does: GET /accounts/{account_id}/tokens/verify（账户令牌；失败时再试 GET /user/tokens/verify 用户令牌）：token 是否有效、是否 active
GET /accounts/{account_id}/warp_connector?per_page=1：能否在这个账户读取 Mesh 节点
GET /accounts/{account_id}/teamnet/routes?per_page=1&is_deleted=false：能否在这个账户读取路由
does_not: 不创建、不修改、不删除任何东西
不能证明写权限：两个列表接口同时接受 Read 与 Write 权限
不读取 token 的权限清单（那需要额外的 API Tokens Read 权限）

how_to: Cloudflare 控制台 → 管理账户 → 账户 API 令牌（Account API Tokens）→ 创建令牌 → 自定义令牌（Cloudflare 要求第一个 API token 在控制台创建）。
权限只加两项，均为账户级：Cloudflare One Connectors · Edit/Write；Cloudflare One Networks · Edit/Write。
账户资源选择要部署 Mesh 的那个账户；不需要任何区域（zone）权限。
可选：设置客户端 IP 过滤为网关的出口 IP、设置到期时间。
创建后把 token 和账户 id（32 位十六进制，在账户首页右侧）填进面板；token 只写不读。

permissions.name: Cloudflare One Connectors Write
permissions.why: 创建、查询、删除 Mesh 节点（warp_connector），读取节点令牌

permissions.name: Cloudflare One Networks Write
permissions.why: 发布、列出、撤回 CIDR 路由（teamnet/routes）

does_not_prove: 隧道真的握手、流量真的经出口出去（端到端连通）
分流结果、DNS / IPv6 / WebRTC 不泄漏（概览「防泄露」只核对生成的配置，要实际执行才算）
流媒体与 AI 服务的解锁（「解锁」页的探测）
远程接入的设备能从外网拨入
independent: 远程接入（开关与设备）是独立资源：保存拓扑、本引导的任何一步都不会打开、关闭或修改它；它的改动随网关的安装生效
Cloudflare Mesh 备路的部署和撤回在 Cloudflare 页，不在本引导里
proves: 在这次运行中实际安装的网关：meridian-host 的安装事务已提交——文件写入、接口与防火墙激活、服务启动，事务里的健康检查通过
在这次运行中实际下发的远端节点：下发脚本完成激活并写下清单，面板在同一登录里读回服务器上的记录，与装上去的内容一致（读回失败、不完整或不一致时这一步是「结果不明」，不算装好）
「已在服务器上（采纳）」：预检完整读到的服务器记录（网关是安装清单）已经是这份内容；没有重新执行，也没有重新检查健康——服务现在是否在运行没有核实

runtime.message: 没有配置 host agent：读不到网关解析器的版本，解析日志保持不可用

covered: 网关上的 SmartDNS 应答的查询，每条一行：时间、发起查询的设备的局域网地址（读到这一行时邻居表里有它时带 MAC）、查询的名字和类型、有没有应答、由哪个解析组应答、耗时、应答里的地址条数（不保存地址本身）
同一个名字被客户端重试时会有多行（一次查询一行），这是正常的
identity: 设备按局域网地址归并，与连接日志相同，备注名也共用同一套；MAC 是读到这一行时内核邻居表里的值
地址可能被换给另一台设备：同一地址在时间范围内出现过不止一个 MAC 时会列出来；从一条记录跳到连接日志（或反过来）时按地址加前后各几分钟的时间窗查找，两边都有 MAC 且不同的记录被排除并计数
MAC 未知（邻居表里没有、读到这一行时已经太晚、远程接入设备本来就没有 MAC）时只能按地址和时间窗关联，界面会标明「仅按地址」
not_covered: 被网关解析器自己的规则直接回答的名字（例如屏蔽的 DoH 域名）：SmartDNS 不为它们写审计行，所以「被规则拦下」不在日志里，也不会被算成别的结果
各出口节点上解析器的查询：这一轮只记录网关上的查询
不经过网关解析器的查询：设备自己用的加密 DNS（DoH / DoT 到别处）、直接写死的地址
解析日志关闭期间、以及解析日志服务停止期间解析器轮转掉的查询
应答的具体地址、上游是哪一台服务器、应答码：审计行里没有应答码
results: 有应答（answered）：这一行带至少一个应答地址
无应答（no_answer）：没有地址，而且在 1.5 秒内返回。名字不存在（NXDOMAIN）是这样；名字存在但没有所问类型的记录、上游很快拒绝也是这样，审计行里没有应答码，分不开
无应答且慢（no_answer_slow）：没有地址，耗时 1.5 秒以上。上游失败或超时是这样（观察到约 2 秒）；很慢的「不存在」也是这样，所以只能说「多半是失败或超时」
被规则拦下的名字不产生任何记录（见上），不是其中任何一类
storage: 只存在网关本机 /var/lib/meridian-dnslog（目录 0700、文件 0600，属 root）：只有 root 能读，面板经宿主代理的固定只读请求查询；不进入拓扑、快照、导出、预检、诊断信息或面板自己的日志
保留最近 24 小时、最多 50000 条；解析器的审计文件及其轮转副本、交接队列和结构化日志合计不超过 32 MiB（审计一侧 8 MiB、队列 2 MiB（内存）、日志 22 MiB），先到的上限生效，超出时删最旧的
写不过来时丢弃日志条目并计数，不影响解析；解析日志服务停止时解析照常，只是不记录
「清空」立即删除网关上的全部记录、轮转副本和审计文件的内容
switch: 默认关闭。日志的内容就是设备查询的名字，所以必须明确打开；打开和关闭都在下一次网关安装（预检 → 确认 → 安装）时生效，预检里能看到解析器配置和服务的差异
打开时安装会重启一次网关解析器（解析中断约一两秒）；关闭时同样重启一次
关闭并安装成功之后，网关上已有的记录全部删除；只保存了关闭、还没有安装（包括取消预检）时仍在记录
只有核对过审计日志行为的 SmartDNS 版本才能打开：解析器容器的镜像标签是 latest，版本可能与核对过的不同，届时这里会说明原因和处理办法

# Resolver bound to the tunnel. Upstream queries use this host's WAN, not the tunnel.
speed-check-mode none
cache-size 4096
bind 10.66.13.2:53
bind-tcp 10.66.13.2:53
bind [fd66:0:0:d::2]:53
bind-tcp [fd66:0:0:d::2]:53
server 1.1.1.1
server 8.8.8.8

# Resolver bound to the tunnel. Upstream queries use this host's WAN, not the tunnel.
speed-check-mode none
cache-size 4096
bind 10.66.14.2:53
bind-tcp 10.66.14.2:53
bind [fd66:0:0:e::2]:53
bind-tcp [fd66:0:0:e::2]:53
server 1.1.1.1
server 8.8.8.8
# external SOCKS exit myext: names are resolved on this carrier, upstream queries over TCP through its proxy
# (1.1.1.1:53, 8.8.8.8:53); no other upstream, no fallback to this host's own servers, no AAAA.
bind [fd66::55:5]:53 -group ext_myext -no-speed-check -no-dualstack-selection -force-aaaa-soa
bind-tcp [fd66::55:5]:53 -group ext_myext -no-speed-check -no-dualstack-selection -force-aaaa-soa
server-tcp 10.66.201.14:5301 -group ext_myext -exclude-default-group
server-tcp 10.66.201.14:5302 -group ext_myext -exclude-default-group

# Resolver bound to the tunnel. Upstream queries use this host's WAN, not the tunnel.
speed-check-mode none
cache-size 4096
bind 10.66.15.2:53
bind-tcp 10.66.15.2:53
bind [fd66:0:0:f::2]:53
bind-tcp [fd66:0:0:f::2]:53
server 1.1.1.1
server 8.8.8.8

# Meridian SmartDNS. Real answers, no fake-ip.
# ECS is intentionally unset so the family prefix is not attached to queries.
# Queries to an exit resolver leave from that exit's WAN, so DNS and the data path share a region.
# A region group the hub switches resolves through its own data path (group mark, group
# resolver address), so its DNS always reaches the member the hub currently uses.
speed-check-mode none
dualstack-ip-selection no
cache-size 65536
cache-persist no
serve-expired yes
rr-ttl-min 60
bind [::]:53
bind-tcp [::]:53
# DoT certificate will not match the name the client dialed. Strict clients fail closed and fall back to port 53.
# The certificate is global in SmartDNS (bind-cert-*); bind-tls takes no certificate options.
bind-cert-file /etc/meridian/dns/cert.pem
bind-cert-key-file /etc/meridian/dns/key.pem
bind-tls [::]:853

# AAAA: clients take IPv6 from the home router, not from this gateway (settings
# clients_ipv6_via_gateway off): IPv6 to a tunnelled name would leave over the home line.
# No AAAA (empty NOERROR, IPv6 hints dropped from HTTPS records) for any name except the
# domestic sets and the rules allowed IPv6, which carry "-address -6".
force-AAAA-SOA yes

server-tls 192.0.2.53:853 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
server 192.0.2.53 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
server-tls 198.51.100.53:853 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
server 198.51.100.53 -group domestic -exclude-default-group

server fd66::54:1 -group g_dc1 -exclude-default-group
server fd66::54:2 -group g_dc2 -exclude-default-group
server fd66::54:3 -group g_gb1 -exclude-default-group
server fd66::54:4 -group g_jp_a -exclude-default-group
server fd66::54:5 -group g_myext -exclude-default-group
server fd66::54:6 -group g_sg1 -exclude-default-group

server fd66::54:8 -group g_us1 -exclude-default-group
server fd66::54:9 -group g_us2 -exclude-default-group

# region groups switched by the hub: the group's resolver address, the group mark on the socket
server fd66::53:a -group rg_gb -exclude-default-group -set-mark 266
server fd66::53:b -group rg_hk -set-mark 267

not_in_scope.what: 承载节点上的外部出口健康检查（meridian-ext-health）
not_in_scope.why: 它在承载节点上运行，结果只在那台节点的本地状态和日志里；网关没有任何现有的固定通道能读到，这一轮不为它在远端节点新增能力

not_in_scope.what: 地区组在枢纽上当前使用哪个成员、何时切换
not_in_scope.why: 由枢纽的故障切换服务决定，面板在需要时经 SSH 读取一次（地区组页面显示的「当前成员」），网关上的采集服务读不到

not_in_scope.instead: 网关经每条路径探测枢纽的结论（承载路径的探测结果）
not_in_scope.what: 中继和枢纽自己的故障切换（中继到枢纽走 IX 还是 WSS、枢纽的回程路径）
not_in_scope.why: 发生在远端节点上，网关读不到

not_in_scope.instead: 网关这一端的握手时间
not_in_scope.what: 隧道对端一侧的握手和链路状态
not_in_scope.why: 只读取网关自己的接口

not_in_scope.what: 解锁探测与出口确认的结果
not_in_scope.why: 由面板按计划或手动发起，结果保存在面板里（解锁页面），不在网关宿主机上，采集服务读不到；这一轮没有把它们转成链路事件

not_in_scope.what: 远程接入（mra）各设备的握手
not_in_scope.why: 那是设备的在线情况，不是链路；链路日志不读取 mra
链路日志不读取连接、名字、地址或设备信息

install: 没有开关：采集服务是每个网关安装内容的一部分，但只在网关安装（预检 → 确认 → 安装）之后才开始运行；面板不会自己在宿主机上启动任何东西
升级到带链路日志的版本之后，网关会显示有待安装的变更：新增 meridian-link-journal.service 和 /etc/meridian/link-journal.json，验收脚本多一段检查；规则集、路由、隧道、解析器配置和故障切换脚本都不变
采集服务只读：不改路由、规则、接口或任何单元；它停止或崩溃时只是不记录
records: 记录的是状态的变化，不是周期性的采样：每条事件有时间、对象、从什么状态到什么状态、依据、之前那个状态持续了多久
事件里只有拓扑里的名字（链路、节点、地区组、接口）、状态和来源给出的原因；不含任何设备地址、域名、连接或其他流量内容
每一类事件都标明依据的强弱：直接读到的状态、网关自己的探测结论、还是间接推断。网关自己的检查失败不等于对端已确认故障
rules: 基线：采集服务第一次读到某个对象时只记下它的状态，不产生事件（不知道这个状态是何时开始的，持续时间按「至少」显示）
重启：状态记在检查点里，重启后状态没变就不产生事件
空窗：采集服务没有运行、某个来源读不到的那段时间记为未知；任何持续时间都不跨过空窗，空窗之后才发现的变化会标明「发生在空窗内，时间不确定」
抖动：同一个对象 10 分钟内的前 4 次变化各记一条，之后的变化合并成一条「变化了 N 次」的记录（保留次数、第一次和最后一次的时间），它不是一次连续的中断；另有每小时最多 600 条的写入上限，超出的丢弃并计数
storage: 只存在网关本机 /var/lib/meridian-linklog（目录 0700、文件 0600，属 root）：只有 root 能读，面板经宿主代理的固定只读请求查询；不进入拓扑、快照、导出、预检或诊断信息
保留最近 30 天、最多 20000 条、合计不超过 16 MiB（事件文件、检查点和它们写入时的临时副本都算在内），先到的上限生效，超出时删最旧的
「清空」立即删除网关上的全部事件和已记下的状态；之后的第一次采集重新建立基线

sources.cadence: 每 10 秒读一次；故障切换服务每 5 秒写一次
sources.events: 网关的境外流量走哪条路径：主链路经哪条腿或哪台中继、切到备用枢纽、切回；以及故障切换服务对路径的探测结论（有应答 / 全部不通 / 勉强承载）
sources.evidence: 切换是故障切换服务自己的决定，读到的就是它记下的结果；「不通 / 勉强承载」是它经每条路径 ping 枢纽的探测结果，不是对流量的直接观察
sources.how: 读网关故障切换服务每一轮写的固定文件 /run/meridian/upstream（限长、按固定格式解析，不执行任何命令）；只有一台中继且没有备用枢纽的网关不写这个文件，改读路由表（见下一行）

sources.class_label: 承载路径（单中继、无备用枢纽）
sources.events: 路由表 102 的默认路由指向哪条腿（UDP / WSS / 家里直连枢纽的 WSS）
sources.evidence: 内核路由表本身；这种拓扑的故障切换服务不记录原因，所以只有切换，没有探测结论和原因
sources.how: 固定参数的只读命令 ip -4 -o route show table 102

sources.events: 某台中继被分担的健康检查剔除、恢复、降权、转为不接新连接，以及它使用的腿和路由表 102 跟随的中继
sources.evidence: 分担控制器自己的状态和原因代码（丢包、时延、送达、吞吐）；控制器不可用时是按能否 ping 通的回退结论，依据里会写明
sources.how: 同一个文件里每台中继的一行（仅多中继分担时有）

sources.events: 每条隧道的握手由正常变为超时（视为不通）、恢复、接口消失
sources.evidence: 内核记录的最近一次握手时间。超过 180 秒没有新的握手才算超时，所以断开最多晚 3 分钟多才记下；只代表网关这一端的会话，对端另有问题时看不出来。关闭了保活的链路不记录
sources.how: 固定参数的只读命令 wg show <接口> latest-handshakes，接口名只取自已安装的对象清单并按受管接口的命名规则校验；从不执行 dump

sources.events: wstunnel 客户端停止 / 运行，以及它承载的隧道握手是否正常（记为连接 / 断开）
sources.evidence: 间接：客户端进程在不在运行，加上它里面的隧道有没有握手成功。WebSocket 会话本身的连接状态没有读取
sources.how: 固定参数的只读命令 systemctl is-active <单元>，单元名只取自对象清单并校验；加上该隧道的握手时间

sources.cadence: 每 30 秒读一次；转发服务每 15 分钟自检一次（启动和规则重载后各一次）
sources.events: 网关对某个外部 SOCKS 出口的自检由通过变为失败、恢复
sources.evidence: 这是「网关经隧道问这个出口的解析器没有得到回答」，不是「代理已经确认不通」：承载节点自己的健康检查网关读不到。开始和结束的时间最多有 15 分钟的误差，短于 15 分钟的中断可能记不到；只有被规则或默认去向直接指向的外部出口才有这项自检，嗅探关闭时没有
sources.how: 读嗅探转发服务状态套接字（只回答 root）的固定请求 GET /v1/health 里最近一次自检的结果

sources.events: 自检里某个目标（地区组、出口、直连）由通过变为失败、恢复
sources.evidence: 转发服务经真实路径问该目标的解析器（默认目标另加一次 TCP 连接）。证明的是那一刻解析器可达，不证明某个网站可用；地区组的结果反映枢纽当时使用的成员

sources.events: 采集空窗（采集服务没有运行、停顿、时钟被调回）、某个来源读不到及恢复、对象清单更新
sources.evidence: 空窗期间的状态记为未知，任何持续时间都不跨过空窗
sources.how: 采集服务自己的两次采集之间的间隔和每个来源的读取结果

not_verified: 预检只证明每一端本机的约束：隧道包从哪块网卡出去、这块网卡（和路由）的 MTU 是多少。路径上更小的 MTU（运营商、隧道、云厂商的网络）看不到：按验证说明用不允许分片的 ping 人工核对
WSS 隧道由 wstunnel 的 TCP 承载：上联 MTU 只决定分段，不会丢包；给出的段数是估算
对端用域名、或对端拨入且拓扑里没有它的固定地址时，按这一端的默认路由判断
采用建议只改拓扑里的 MTU 字段；要在部署页预检、审阅每个节点的变更并确认后才会下发

modes.full: 全隧道模式：手机的全部 IPv4/IPv6 流量和 DNS 都进隧道，由网关按家里局域网的规则处理：国内直连（从家里宽带出去）、境外走 Meridian 隧道、未分类拒绝，DNS 只能用网关。设备之间不能互访；面板只对家里局域网开放。
modes.home: 仅家网模式：只有家里局域网的地址和网关的 DNS 地址走隧道。手机访问公网仍走它当前的网络（蜂窝或别处的 Wi-Fi），不经过 Meridian，国内直连、境外走隧道和防泄漏规则都不作用于这部分流量；DNS 是否全部交给网关取决于手机系统，部分查询可能仍走当前网络的 DNS。要让 Meridian 接管全部流量请用全隧道模式。

body.shared_address: 网关按解析出的目的地址分流：两个指向不同目标的名字解析到同一个地址时，该地址按列表里更靠前的规则走。
upgrade_notes: 升级后，苹果和各系统的联网检测域名不再内置直连：没有规则指向直连时，它们和其它境外域名一样由默认组（或命中规则的目标）的解析器解析并走隧道。需要直连就启用「Apple 直连」模板或加一条直连规则。
升级后，靠前的规则优先于更长的后缀：以前解析器按“最长的名字”在规则之间选，现在按列表顺序第一条命中。结果因此改变的规则在「遮蔽」列标为“升级后变化”。
「未列名单的域名也问国内 DNS」默认关闭，规则和国内名单都不依赖它。

address_only: 所有 UDP，包括 QUIC（UDP 443 仍由「走隧道的流量拒绝 UDP 443」开关处理）
不在接管列表里的 TCP 端口
读不到名字的 TCP：没有 SNI、SNI 是地址、HTTP/2 明文前言、非 TLS/HTTP 协议、服务器先说话的协议、超时、畸形或超长
带 ECH 且明文名字是已知 ECH 公共名（默认 cloudflare-ech.com）的连接：真名字被加密，按目的地址
目的是本机、局域网、私有地址、远程接入地址池或已知 DoH 地址的连接（不接管）
接管之前已经建立的连接（只接管新连接的第一个 SYN）
读到了名字、但目标的解析器给不出地址的连接（名字不存在、没有可用地址、解析器全部失败或 3 秒内没有结果）：按目的地址和分类链的结果，不用名字规则的去向
by_name: 局域网和远程接入设备新建的 TCP 连接，目的端口在接管列表里（默认 80、443），并且客户端在 1 秒内发出了 TLS ClientHello 的 SNI 或 HTTP/1 的 Host：按名字在有序规则表里自上而下匹配（关键词规则按子串生效），再由目标自己的解析器重新解析后连接
costs: 带 ECH 扩展、明文名字不在公共名列表里的连接按明文名字判断：浏览器发的 GREASE ECH 时这就是真名字；真正启用 ECH 而提供方的公共名不在列表里时，会按那个公共名分流（通常落到默认组）
按名字判断的连接连接的是目标解析器给的地址，不是客户端自己解析到的地址
所有被接管的连接经过网关上的用户态转发，占用网关的 CPU 和内存，并增加约一个往返的建立时延（服务器先说话的协议多等 1 秒）
服务停止或崩溃时被接管的连接直接失败，不会回落到按地址的路径
中继被淘汰时，转发服务已建立的连接不会像转发流量那样被立即重置，而是留在原中继上直到结束；新连接按新的权重分配

body.message: 没有配置 host agent，读不到嗅探服务的连接日志

covered: 局域网和远程接入设备新建的、发往接管端口（默认 80、443）的 TCP 连接，也就是嗅探服务经手的每一条：开始时间、时长、来源地址（能取到时带 MAC）、原目的地址和端口、实际连接的地址、协议、判断依据（按名字 / 按地址及原因）、命中的规则、去向、结果、结束方式和原因、双向字节数（只有数量，没有内容）
lifecycle: 每条连接在结束时写一条记录（拒绝、连接失败的立即结束；转发中的在任一方关闭、重置、空闲 2 小时或服务停止时结束），列表按结束时间排列，一条连接只算一次
仍在转发的连接不在记录和统计里，显示在设备的「正在转发」中（每台设备最多列 50 条），结束后才成为一条记录
嗅探服务正常停止或重启（例如安装新版本）时，仍打开的连接以「服务停止时中断」写入；被强行终止（kill、崩溃、断电）时这些连接没有记录，下次启动会提示一次，并给出当时（最近一分钟内）还开着的连接数
names_off: 未记录名字：日志不保存任何名字（也不保存其散列），只有地址、端口和判断结果
names_on: 已开启名字记录：每条记录还保存嗅探读到的名字（TLS 的 SNI、HTTP 的 Host，带 ECH 时是明文的外层名）
名字与目的地址一起保留 24 小时（最多 50000 条），只在网关本机；随时可以「清空日志」
关闭名字记录并安装后，嗅探服务重启时删掉日志里已有的全部名字，其余字段保留
not_covered: 所有 UDP，包括 QUIC：不经过嗅探服务，没有按连接的记录
不在接管列表里的 TCP 端口，以及不接管的目的地址（本机、局域网、私有地址、远程接入地址池、已知 DoH）
嗅探关闭、嗅探服务停止期间的全部流量
接管之前已经建立的连接
DNS 查询：不在连接日志里。设备解析了哪些名字由单独的「解析日志」记录（默认关闭，需要明确打开）
results: 成功：上游连上并且至少有一个字节从上游回到客户端（之后怎样结束都算成功，结束方式另列）
失败：解析失败、连接失败（附原因：超时 / 被拒绝 / 网络不可达 / 没有路由 / 被重置 / 地址族不可用 / 被本机拒绝 / 其它，以及最后尝试的地址）、连上后被重置或出错、连上后无回应（客户端发了数据但上游没有回任何字节就结束，包括空闲超时）、分类标记问题、服务停止时中断、其它
不算失败：被规则拒绝（规则按设计拦下）、客户端关闭（还没判断就关闭，或连上后既没发数据也没收到数据就离开，例如预连接）、结束情况未知（旧版本在连上时就记为成功的记录）
storage: 只存在网关本机 /var/lib/meridian-sniff（目录 0700、文件 0600，属嗅探服务账号）：只有 root 和嗅探服务自己能读，面板经宿主代理的固定只读请求查询
保留最近 24 小时（按连接结束的时间）、最多 50000 条，连同轮转文件不超过 32 MiB；超出时删除最旧的；写不过来时丢弃日志条目并计数，从不影响连接
不进入拓扑、快照、导出、诊断信息或面板自己的日志；关闭嗅探（下次安装移除嗅探服务）时整个日志目录随之删除
「清空日志」立即删除网关上的全部记录（连同嗅探服务内存里最近结束的连接）；正在转发的连接不是记录，结束后照常写入

catalog.basis: 自制剧标题页 81280792：403 = 拒绝该 IP；404 = 标题不可用（仅自制剧或未开通）；200 时取目录地区：URL 的 /xx-yy/ 国家前缀（非美国出口上重定向到 /hk-en/ 这类路径；只有语言的 /ja、/en 不算地区），没有国家前缀时读页面内嵌数据里访问者所在国家的 "requestCountry":{…"id":"XX"…}（只认 requestCountry 对象自己的 id，相距有界）；地区必须与出口地区一致；前缀和 requestCountry 同时存在但不一致、或页面里有多处取值不同的 requestCountry = 冲突 = 未知；两者都没有 = 未知；不读 countryCode，也不读 preferredLocale / locale / geo 的 supportedLocales 里的国家（那是偏好或列表，不是访问者所在地）。这一步的正文读取上限是 2 MiB（默认是 256 KiB）；读到上限还有正文且没有标记时仍是未知，证据写明正文被截断和读了多少
catalog.limits: 公开脚本带浏览器 Cookie 并比较自制剧与非自制剧两个标题，本适配器不带 Cookie、只看一个自制剧标题，所以“仅自制剧”与“完全解锁”不区分；页面结构变化会落到未知；2026-11-15 在真实平台上的观察（只是观察）：香港出口上整页约 690 KB，页面内嵌数据里 "requestCountry":{"supportedLocales":["zh","en"],"id":"HK",…} 在约 454,000 字节处（三处相邻），旁边还有 geo.supportedLocales、preferredLocale（id 为 en-HK）和 "currentCountry":null，页面里没有 countryCode；香港、台湾出口靠 URL 前缀（/hk-en/、/tw-en/、/jp-en/ 这类重定向）判定，已在真实出口上用过；美国出口没有重定向也没有前缀，此前报未知（只读了前 256 KiB，正文被截断），所以这一步单独放宽到 2 MiB（硬上限 4 MiB 以内，其他检测项不变），代价有界：每个出口每个地址族一次请求，最多读 2 MiB，超时不变，页面再变大、标记落到上限之外时报未知（正文被截断）；已移除通用 countryCode 作为地区依据（它在页面里可能有别的含义）；没有直接观察过美国出口上 requestCountry 的结构，美国这一情形的修改后尚未在真实平台上复测，仍标为未对真实平台验证

body.ingest_rule: unlocked = 成功，not_unlocked = 失败；network_ok / unknown / failed 不是解锁结论，按 inconclusive 入库，既不降级也不恢复；not_applicable（检测方法不支持这个地址族，没有发出请求）不入库

reasons.discontinued: 平台已停止或并入别的服务，公开方法已过时
reasons.fake_login: 公开方法提交伪造的登录表单看错误码，本项目不提交任何登录请求
reasons.header_only: 判断依据在应答头或 Set-Cookie 里，探测不把应答头和 Cookie 交给分类器
reasons.needs_js: 公开方法要执行页面脚本，或从主机不固定的脚本里抓参数，放不进固定主机名单
reasons.needs_token: 公开方法要把账号、应用令牌、API key、播放器 policy key、设备标识或会话值当作请求参数，本项目不发送任何这类数据
reasons.not_https: 公开方法用明文 HTTP 或非 443 端口，探测只走 https/443
reasons.not_service: 不是流媒体或 AI 服务（地区识别、IP 信誉、CDN 位置、游戏、论坛），不是解锁判断；出口确认已经给出实际地区
reasons.transport: 公开方法降低 TLS 要求（允许旧式重协商）或直连写死的 IP 并改写 Host 头，探测不这样做
reasons.weak_signal: 只有不可靠的判断依据（写死的地区表、只看 HTTP 状态码（403 也可能是风控）、页面里的单个字样、第三方地理服务、只能读出地区而没有任何不可用标记）

body.validation_text: 检测规则依据公开检测方法与合成样本编写，本项目尚未在真实平台上验证；真实平台行为待人工核对。

catalog.basis: 自制剧标题页 81280792：403 = 拒绝该 IP；404 = 标题不可用（仅自制剧或未开通）；200 时取目录地区：URL 的 /xx-yy/ 国家前缀（非美国出口上重定向到 /hk-en/ 这类路径；只有语言的 /ja、/en 不算地区），没有国家前缀时读页面内嵌数据里访问者所在国家的 "requestCountry":{…"id":"XX"…}（只认 requestCountry 对象自己的 id，相距有界）；地区必须与出口地区一致；前缀和 requestCountry 同时存在但不一致、或页面里有多处取值不同的 requestCountry = 冲突 = 未知；两者都没有 = 未知；不读 countryCode，也不读 preferredLocale / locale / geo 的 supportedLocales 里的国家（那是偏好或列表，不是访问者所在地）。这一步的正文读取上限是 2 MiB（默认是 256 KiB）；读到上限还有正文且没有标记时仍是未知，证据写明正文被截断和读了多少
catalog.limits: 公开脚本带浏览器 Cookie 并比较自制剧与非自制剧两个标题，本适配器不带 Cookie、只看一个自制剧标题，所以“仅自制剧”与“完全解锁”不区分；页面结构变化会落到未知；2026-11-15 在真实平台上的观察（只是观察）：香港出口上整页约 690 KB，页面内嵌数据里 "requestCountry":{"supportedLocales":["zh","en"],"id":"HK",…} 在约 454,000 字节处（三处相邻），旁边还有 geo.supportedLocales、preferredLocale（id 为 en-HK）和 "currentCountry":null，页面里没有 countryCode；香港、台湾出口靠 URL 前缀（/hk-en/、/tw-en/、/jp-en/ 这类重定向）判定，已在真实出口上用过；美国出口没有重定向也没有前缀，此前报未知（只读了前 256 KiB，正文被截断），所以这一步单独放宽到 2 MiB（硬上限 4 MiB 以内，其他检测项不变），代价有界：每个出口每个地址族一次请求，最多读 2 MiB，超时不变，页面再变大、标记落到上限之外时报未知（正文被截断）；已移除通用 countryCode 作为地区依据（它在页面里可能有别的含义）；没有直接观察过美国出口上 requestCountry 的结构，美国这一情形的修改后尚未在真实平台上复测，仍标为未对真实平台验证

catalog.limits: 公开脚本的完整方法要用 bamgrid 设备令牌（应用令牌）调 GraphQL，本项目不使用任何令牌，只用首页跳转与页面内嵌的 location；location 这一键不在公开脚本里，是 2026-11-15 在真实平台上的观察（首页约 1.95 MB，"location":"XX" 在约 860 KB 处，与实际出口地区一致，后面紧跟 "pageId":"welcome","region":"us"；这个 region 是固定值，从香港访问时也是 us，页面里没有 countryCode），所以只认 "location" 紧跟 "pageId" 的写法，键的顺序或名字一变就是未知，不会误判；URL 语言-地区前缀不在公开脚本的方法里，不可靠，已不再使用；上限 2 MiB 够到约 860 KB 处的标记，代价有界：每个出口每个地址族一次请求，最多读 2 MiB，超时不变；页面再变大、标记落到上限之外时报未知（正文被截断）；修改后尚未在真实平台上复测，仍标为未对真实平台验证

catalog.basis: Premium 介绍页（请求带公开方法里的固定同意 Cookie SOCS 和英文 Accept-Language）：先看同意页——跳到 consent.youtube.com / consent.google.com，或页面是指向它们的同意表单（Before you continue to YouTube）= 未知·同意页，即使页面里有 ad-free 也不算可用；再看引用 www.google.cn = 不可用（cn）；含 Premium is not available in your country（不分大小写）= 不可用；含 ad-free（不分大小写）= 可用，INNERTUBE_CONTEXT_GL 给出的地区只作展示；其他 = 未知。这一步的正文读取上限是 2 MiB（默认是 256 KiB）；读到上限还有正文且没有任何判定标记时仍是未知，证据写明正文被截断和读了多少
catalog.limits: 只带来源里公开的固定同意值（SOCS），不带来源里同一请求的访客 / 会话标识 Cookie（YSC、VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE、VISITOR_PRIVACY_METADATA、__Secure-YEC、__Secure-BUCKET、PREF：那是某个浏览器的标识，不属于本项目）；Cookie 只发给 www.youtube.com / youtube.com，同意页主机不在固定主机里，不跟随；同意值被平台拒绝时仍会得到同意页，记为未知·同意页；只读未登录的介绍页，不是账号判断；2026-11-15 在真实平台上看到介绍页约 1 MB，ad-free 第一次出现在约 850 KB 处（页面最后五分之一，后面还有二十多处），INNERTUBE_CONTEXT_GL 在约 60 KB 处，带不带同意 Cookie 都一样——此前各出口的未知是正文只读了 256 KiB、被截断造成的，不是页面改版，也与同意 Cookie 无关，所以这一步单独放宽到 2 MiB；代价有界：每个出口每个地址族一次请求，最多读 2 MiB，超时不变；页面再变大超过上限时报未知（正文被截断）；2026-11-15 用此 Cookie 和 2 MiB 上限在真实平台上复测，六个出口判为可用且地区正确（不可用地区的应答仍未核实）

body.interruption: 每次在一端安装新阶段时，这端的 wstunnel 会重启，这条 WSS 承载中断几秒；两端始终处于相邻阶段，所以不会因为只更新了一端而断开。
body.order: 轮换顺序：服务端与客户端交替各下发约两次（面板列出下一步）；任一端失败会补偿回旧文件，旧凭据继续可用。
body.verification: wstunnel 11.1.0 没有指纹固定选项：客户端开启 --tls-verify-certificate，SSL_CERT_FILE 只含该监听的自签证书（唯一信任根），并按合成名称校验（--tls-sni-override）。

+# Publish order: NAT dial-out exits, other exits, hub, relay, gateway.
+# IX is a dedicated line, not a host. Mesh is not in this list.
+# Region groups resolve through fd66::53:0/112 on their members: publish the exits
+# (and the hub) before the gateway. A gateway installed first gets no answer for
+# group names until the member in use is re-published; it never falls back to
+# another resolver.
+1	twnat
+2	dc1
+3	dc2
+4	gb1
+5	jp-a
+6	sg1
+7	us1
+8	us2
+9	hkb
+10	ix
+11	access
+12	access2
+13	gw

+#!/usr/sbin/nft -f
+# Transit node. Does not NAT client traffic and does not own the default route.
+table inet meridian
+delete table inet meridian
+table inet meridian {
+  chain ingress_return_in {
+    type filter hook prerouting priority mangle; policy accept;
+    iifname "m02" ct direction original ct mark set 0x4e00 comment "arrived from gw"
+    iifname "m02w" ct direction original ct mark set 0x4e01 comment "arrived from gw"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4e00 meta mark set 0x4e00 comment "reply: back into m02"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4e01 meta mark set 0x4e01 comment "reply: back into m02w"
+  }
+  chain ingress_return_out {
+    type route hook output priority mangle; policy accept;
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4e00 meta mark set 0x4e00 comment "local reply: back into m02"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4e01 meta mark set 0x4e01 comment "local reply: back into m02w"
+  }
+  chain speedtest_in {
+    type filter hook input priority filter - 5; policy accept;
+    iifname "m02" ip saddr 10.66.3.1 ip daddr 10.66.3.2 tcp dport 9277 accept comment "speed test: the gateway on this leg only"
+    iifname "m02w" ip saddr 10.66.102.1 ip daddr 10.66.102.2 tcp dport 9277 accept comment "speed test: the gateway on this leg only"
+    tcp dport 9277 drop comment "speed-test endpoint: nothing else (public, LAN, forwarded, IPv6)"
+  }
+  chain input {
+    type filter hook input priority filter; policy accept;
+    iifname "eth0" udp dport { 51823 } drop comment "wss wireguard port is reached only via local wstunnel"
+  }
+  chain tunnel_mss_out {

+    oifname { "m00", "m02", "m02w" } tcp flags syn meta nfproto ipv6 tcp option maxseg size > 1300 tcp option maxseg size set 1300
+  }
+  chain tunnel_mss_in {

===== nodes/access/etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf (added) =====
+# Meridian host sysctls. Does not flush other sysctls.
+# Forwarding is NOT turned on here: systemd-sysctl applies this file at
+# boot, before meridian.service has loaded the nft guard. meridian-up.sh
+# enables forwarding from /etc/meridian/forwarding.conf after the firewall
+# (and on the gateway the inet meridian_guard table) is loaded.
+# Remote node: only the topology's interface and the one global that is
+# required (send_redirects is ORed with all). all/default rp_filter and
+# accept_redirects are left to the host.
+net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects=0
+net.ipv4.conf.eth0.rp_filter=2
+net.ipv4.conf.eth0.send_redirects=0
+net.ipv4.conf.eth0.accept_redirects=0
+net.ipv6.conf.eth0.accept_redirects=0

===== nodes/access/usr/local/sbin/meridian-failover.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# IX replacement is pre-provisioned. It takes traffic only after health failure or when IX_MODE=1.
+set -u
+IX_MODE=0
+WEST_UDP="m02"
+WEST_WSS="m02w"
+EAST_IX="m00"
+EAST_WSS=""
+WEST_PEER_UDP="10.66.3.1"
+WEST_PEER_WSS="10.66.102.1"
+EAST_PEER_IX="10.66.1.2"
+EAST_PEER_WSS=""
+LAN="192.168.77.0/24"
+TRANSIT4="10.66.200.0/24"
+TRANSIT6="fd66:0:0:ff::/64"
+LAN6="2001:db8:77::/64"
+FAILS_NEED=3
+RECOVERS_NEED=5
+COOLDOWN=120
+state=/run/meridian/relay-failover
+mkdir -p /run/meridian
+
+alive() {
+  local iface="$1" peer="$2"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 1
+  ping -I "$iface" -c 1 -W 2 -n "$peer" >/dev/null 2>&1
+}
+apply_east() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 0
+  ip route replace default dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 150
+  ip -6 route replace default dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 150
+  ip -6 route replace fd66::/48 dev "$iface"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767
+}
+apply_west() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 0
+  ip route replace "$LAN" dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace "$TRANSIT4" dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace "$LAN" dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace "$TRANSIT4" dev "$iface" table 150
+  if [ -n "$LAN6" ]; then
+    ip -6 route replace "$LAN6" dev "$iface"
+    ip -6 route replace "$LAN6" dev "$iface" table 150
+  fi
+  ip -6 route replace "$TRANSIT6" dev "$iface"
+  ip -6 route replace "$TRANSIT6" dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace blackhole "$LAN" metric 32767
+  ip route replace blackhole "$TRANSIT4" metric 32767
+  ip route replace blackhole 10.66.0.0/16 metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole "$TRANSIT6" metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767
+  if [ -n "$LAN6" ]; then
+    ip -6 route replace blackhole "$LAN6" metric 32767
+  fi
+}
+east_pref="$EAST_IX"
+[ "$IX_MODE" = "1" ] && east_pref="$EAST_WSS"
+west_pref="$WEST_UDP"
+[ -n "$west_pref" ] || west_pref="$WEST_WSS"
+cur_east="$east_pref"
+cur_west="$west_pref"
+east_bad=0
+west_bad=0
+last_switch=0
+# Self-heal: rule priority 18100 is the first one meridian-routes.sh adds.
+RULE_SENTINEL=18100
+rule_missing=0
+rule_heal() {
+  local rules
+  rules=$(ip rule show 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  if printf '%s\n' "$rules" | grep -q "^$RULE_SENTINEL:"; then rule_missing=0; return 0; fi
+  rule_missing=$((rule_missing + 1))
+  [ "$rule_missing" -ge 2 ] || return 0
+  if /usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-rule-heal: policy rule $RULE_SENTINEL was missing; re-ran meridian-routes.sh, restarting the failover loop" >&2
+    exec "$0"
+  fi
+  if [ "$rule_missing" -eq 2 ]; then echo "meridian-rule-heal: policy rule $RULE_SENTINEL is missing and meridian-routes.sh failed; retrying every 5 s" >&2; fi
+  return 0
+}
+while true; do

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-563f4d9c
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m02 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m02"
+  "-i m02w -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m02w"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).

+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"

+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_RA_STATE=/var/lib/meridian/node/ra-accept
+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" ]; then ra_old=$(cat "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"); fi
+for ra_if in $(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ra_now" "$ra_old" | sort -u); do

+    1)

+#!/bin/bash
+# IX replacement is pre-provisioned. It takes traffic only after health failure or when IX_MODE=1.
+set -u
+IX_MODE=0
+WEST_UDP="m03"
+WEST_WSS=""
+EAST_IX="m01"
+EAST_WSS=""
+WEST_PEER_UDP="10.66.4.1"
+WEST_PEER_WSS=""
+EAST_PEER_IX="10.66.2.2"
+EAST_PEER_WSS=""
+LAN="192.168.77.0/24"
+TRANSIT4="10.66.200.0/24"
+TRANSIT6="fd66:0:0:ff::/64"
+LAN6="2001:db8:77::/64"
+FAILS_NEED=3
+RECOVERS_NEED=5
+COOLDOWN=120
+state=/run/meridian/relay-failover
+mkdir -p /run/meridian
+
+alive() {
+  local iface="$1" peer="$2"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 1
+  ping -I "$iface" -c 1 -W 2 -n "$peer" >/dev/null 2>&1
+}
+apply_east() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 0
+  ip route replace default dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 150
+  ip -6 route replace default dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 150
+  ip -6 route replace fd66::/48 dev "$iface"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767
+}
+apply_west() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 0
+  ip route replace "$LAN" dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace "$TRANSIT4" dev "$iface"
+  ip route replace "$LAN" dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace "$TRANSIT4" dev "$iface" table 150
+  if [ -n "$LAN6" ]; then
+    ip -6 route replace "$LAN6" dev "$iface"
+    ip -6 route replace "$LAN6" dev "$iface" table 150
+  fi
+  ip -6 route replace "$TRANSIT6" dev "$iface"
+  ip -6 route replace "$TRANSIT6" dev "$iface" table 150
+  ip route replace blackhole "$LAN" metric 32767
+  ip route replace blackhole "$TRANSIT4" metric 32767
+  ip route replace blackhole 10.66.0.0/16 metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole "$TRANSIT6" metric 32767
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767
+  if [ -n "$LAN6" ]; then
+    ip -6 route replace blackhole "$LAN6" metric 32767
+  fi
+}
+east_pref="$EAST_IX"
+[ "$IX_MODE" = "1" ] && east_pref="$EAST_WSS"
+west_pref="$WEST_UDP"
+[ -n "$west_pref" ] || west_pref="$WEST_WSS"
+cur_east="$east_pref"
+cur_west="$west_pref"
+east_bad=0
+west_bad=0
+last_switch=0
+# Self-heal: rule priority 18100 is the first one meridian-routes.sh adds.
+RULE_SENTINEL=18100
+rule_missing=0
+rule_heal() {
+  local rules
+  rules=$(ip rule show 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  if printf '%s\n' "$rules" | grep -q "^$RULE_SENTINEL:"; then rule_missing=0; return 0; fi
+  rule_missing=$((rule_missing + 1))
+  [ "$rule_missing" -ge 2 ] || return 0
+  if /usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-rule-heal: policy rule $RULE_SENTINEL was missing; re-ran meridian-routes.sh, restarting the failover loop" >&2
+    exec "$0"
+  fi
+  if [ "$rule_missing" -eq 2 ]; then echo "meridian-rule-heal: policy rule $RULE_SENTINEL is missing and meridian-routes.sh failed; retrying every 5 s" >&2; fi
+  return 0
+}
+while true; do
+  rule_heal
+  now=$(date +%s)
+  want_east="$EAST_IX"
+  if [ "$IX_MODE" = "1" ]; then
+    if alive "$EAST_WSS" "$EAST_PEER_WSS"; then want_east="$EAST_WSS"
+    elif alive "$EAST_IX" "$EAST_PEER_IX"; then want_east="$EAST_IX"
+    else want_east="$EAST_WSS"; fi
+  else
+    if alive "$EAST_IX" "$EAST_PEER_IX"; then want_east="$EAST_IX"
+    elif alive "$EAST_WSS" "$EAST_PEER_WSS"; then want_east="$EAST_WSS"
+    else want_east="$EAST_IX"; fi
+  fi
+  want_west="$WEST_UDP"
+  if alive "$WEST_UDP" "$WEST_PEER_UDP"; then want_west="$WEST_UDP"
+  elif alive "$WEST_WSS" "$WEST_PEER_WSS"; then want_west="$WEST_WSS"
+  fi
+  if [ "$want_east" != "$cur_east" ]; then
+    east_bad=$((east_bad+1))
+    if [ "$east_bad" -ge "$FAILS_NEED" ] && [ $((now-last_switch)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" -o "$last_switch" -eq 0 ]; then
+      apply_east "$want_east"
+      cur_east="$want_east"
+      east_bad=0
+      last_switch=$now
+    fi
+  else
+    east_bad=0
+  fi
+  if [ "$want_west" != "$cur_west" ]; then
+    west_bad=$((west_bad+1))
+    if [ "$west_bad" -ge "$FAILS_NEED" ]; then
+      apply_west "$want_west"
+      cur_west="$want_west"
+      west_bad=0
+    fi
+  else
+    west_bad=0
+  fi
+  sleep 5
+done

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-b0266c70
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m03 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m03"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Policy routes for one Meridian node. Safe to re-run.
+# fd66::/48 is never given a next hop of the ROS gateway.
+set -euo pipefail
+del_rule() {
+  while "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; do :; done || true
+}
+# rp_filter=2 and no ICMP redirects on Meridian's interfaces only (the
+# managed tunnels, the interface the topology names, mra/mmesh). The kernel
+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the
+# interface value is what matters here. Other interfaces are not touched.
+harden_sysctl() {
+  local i
+  for i in "$@"; do
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.rp_filter=2" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.send_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv6.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  done
+}
+harden_sysctl eth0 m01 m03
+# meridian-east-preferred: ix m01
+ip route replace 192.168.77.0/24 dev m03
+ip route replace 10.66.200.0/24 dev m03

+ip -6 route replace fd66:0:0:ff::/64 dev m03

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=any
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_RA_STATE=/var/lib/meridian/node/ra-accept
+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" ]; then ra_old=$(cat "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"); fi
+for ra_if in $(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ra_now" "$ra_old" | sort -u); do
+  case "$ra_if" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) continue ;; esac
+  ra_f=/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra
+  [ -r "$ra_f" ] || continue
+  ra_cur=$(head -c 8 "$ra_f")
+  case "$ra_cur" in
+    2) ;;
+    1)
+      if ! sysctl -w "net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra=2" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-ra-failed: could not set accept_ra=2 on $ra_if; IPv6 forwarding not enabled" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      echo "meridian-ra: $ra_if accept_ra 1 -> 2 (keeps its router advertisements with IPv6 forwarding on)" ;;
+    *)
+      case " $(printf '%s ' $ra_now) " in
+        *" $ra_if "*)
+          echo "meridian-ra-unmanaged: $ra_if has RA-learned IPv6 routes but accept_ra=$ra_cur (a userspace RA client); IPv6 forwarding could break it, so forwarding is not enabled" >&2
+          exit 1 ;;
+      esac
+      continue ;;
+  esac
+  install -d -m 700 "${MERIDIAN_RA_STATE%/*}"
+  grep -qx -- "$ra_if" "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$ra_if" >> "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"
+done

+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1

+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+# The MTU each tunnel interface's config sets ("MTU ="): wg syncconf keeps the
+# running interface MTU, so an existing interface is aligned in place below.
+wg_conf_mtu() {
+  case "$1" in
+    m01) echo 1420 ;;
+    m03) echo 1420 ;;
+    *) echo "" ;;
+  esac
+}
+for iface in m01 m03; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"

+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2

+    fi

+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi

+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+if [ -e /lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ] || [ -e /usr/lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ]; then
+  nd=/etc/systemd/networkd.conf.d/90-meridian.conf
+  nd_want='# meridian: keep Meridian ip rules and routes when systemd-networkd restarts
+[Network]
+ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=no
+ManageForeignRoutes=no'

+    if mkdir -p "${nd%/*}" && printf '%s\n' "$nd_want" > "$nd.tmp" && chmod 0644 "$nd.tmp" && mv -f "$nd.tmp" "$nd"; then
+      echo "meridian-networkd: wrote $nd (networkd not restarted; it applies at its next start)"
+    else
+      rm -f "$nd.tmp"
+      echo "meridian-networkd: could not write $nd; a networkd restart would delete the Meridian ip rules" >&2
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh

+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2

+    iifname { "m05", "m12" } ip6 daddr fd66::53:0/112 tcp dport 53 dnat ip6 to fd66:0:0:d::2 comment "region-group resolver addresses: this exit's tunnel resolver"
+  }
+  chain hub_return_in {
+    type filter hook prerouting priority mangle; policy accept;
+    iifname "m12" ct direction original ct mark set 0x4d50 comment "arrived from the primary hub ix"
+    iifname "m05" ct direction original ct mark set 0x4d51 comment "arrived from the backup hub hkb"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d50 meta mark set 0x4d50 comment "reply: back through the primary hub"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d51 meta mark set 0x4d51 comment "reply: back through the backup hub"
+  }
+  chain hub_return_out {

+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d50 meta mark set 0x4d50 comment "local reply (resolver, ping): back through the primary hub"

===== nodes/dc1/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-c289f476
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m05 -o m19"
+  "-i m19 -o m05"
+  "-i m12 -o m19"
+  "-i m19 -o m12"
+  "-i m05 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m05 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m12 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m12 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the

+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.send_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='dc1'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"

+: > "$raw6"

+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_RA_STATE=/var/lib/meridian/node/ra-accept
+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" ]; then ra_old=$(cat "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"); fi
+for ra_if in $(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ra_now" "$ra_old" | sort -u); do
+  case "$ra_if" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) continue ;; esac
+  ra_f=/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra
+  [ -r "$ra_f" ] || continue
+  ra_cur=$(head -c 8 "$ra_f")
+  case "$ra_cur" in
+    2) ;;
+    1)
+      if ! sysctl -w "net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra=2" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-ra-failed: could not set accept_ra=2 on $ra_if; IPv6 forwarding not enabled" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      echo "meridian-ra: $ra_if accept_ra 1 -> 2 (keeps its router advertisements with IPv6 forwarding on)" ;;
+    *)
+      case " $(printf '%s ' $ra_now) " in
+        *" $ra_if "*)
+          echo "meridian-ra-unmanaged: $ra_if has RA-learned IPv6 routes but accept_ra=$ra_cur (a userspace RA client); IPv6 forwarding could break it, so forwarding is not enabled" >&2
+          exit 1 ;;
+      esac
+      continue ;;
+  esac
+  install -d -m 700 "${MERIDIAN_RA_STATE%/*}"
+  grep -qx -- "$ra_if" "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$ra_if" >> "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"
+done
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+# The MTU each tunnel interface's config sets ("MTU ="): wg syncconf keeps the
+# running interface MTU, so an existing interface is aligned in place below.
+wg_conf_mtu() {
+  case "$1" in
+    m05) echo 1420 ;;
+    m12) echo 1420 ;;
+    m19) echo 1420 ;;
+    *) echo "" ;;
+  esac
+}
+for iface in m05 m12 m19; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+    want_mtu=$(wg_conf_mtu "$iface")
+    have_mtu=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$iface/mtu" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [ -n "$want_mtu" ] && [ "$have_mtu" != "$want_mtu" ]; then
+      ip link set dev "$iface" mtu "$want_mtu"
+      echo "meridian-wg-mtu: $iface ${have_mtu:-?} -> $want_mtu (set in place; the tunnel stays up)"
+    fi
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+if [ -e /lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ] || [ -e /usr/lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ]; then
+  nd=/etc/systemd/networkd.conf.d/90-meridian.conf
+  nd_want='# meridian: keep Meridian ip rules and routes when systemd-networkd restarts
+[Network]
+ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=no
+ManageForeignRoutes=no'
+  if [ "$(cat "$nd" 2>/dev/null)" != "$nd_want" ]; then
+    if mkdir -p "${nd%/*}" && printf '%s\n' "$nd_want" > "$nd.tmp" && chmod 0644 "$nd.tmp" && mv -f "$nd.tmp" "$nd"; then
+      echo "meridian-networkd: wrote $nd (networkd not restarted; it applies at its next start)"
+    else
+      rm -f "$nd.tmp"
+      echo "meridian-networkd: could not write $nd; a networkd restart would delete the Meridian ip rules" >&2
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit meridian-unlock.timer
+if [ -f /etc/smartdns/smartdns.conf ] && [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  if systemctl cat meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    systemctl enable meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    systemctl restart meridian-smartdns.service || echo "meridian-smartdns.service restart failed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  else
+    echo "meridian-smartdns.service is not installed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  fi
+fi
+echo meridian-up-complete

+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d50 meta mark set 0x4d50 comment "reply: back through the primary hub"
+    ct direction reply ct mark 0x4d51 meta mark set 0x4d51 comment "reply: back through the backup hub"

+  chain hub_return_out {

+  chain exit_dns {
+    type nat hook prerouting priority dstnat; policy accept;
+    iifname { "m13", "m06" } ip6 daddr fd66::54:2 udp dport 53 dnat ip6 to fd66:0:0:e::2 comment "this exit's resolver address, from either hub"

+    iifname { "m06", "m13" } ip6 saddr fd66:0:0:ff::e ip6 daddr fd66::55:5 tcp dport 53 accept comment "external exit myext: pinned probe DNS only"
+    iifname { "m06", "m13" } ip6 saddr fd66:0:0:ff::e ip6 daddr fd66::53:0/112 udp dport 53 dnat ip6 to [fd66::55:5]:53 comment "external exit myext: region-group queries, answered by its resolver group here"
+    iifname { "m06", "m13" } ip6 saddr fd66:0:0:ff::e ip6 daddr fd66::53:0/112 tcp dport 53 dnat ip6 to [fd66::55:5]:53 comment "external exit myext: region-group queries, answered by its resolver group here"
+    iifname { "m06", "m13" } ip6 daddr fd66::54:5 udp dport 53 dnat ip6 to [fd66::55:5]:53 comment "external exit myext: its resolver address, from either hub"
+    iifname { "m06", "m13" } ip6 daddr fd66::54:5 tcp dport 53 dnat ip6 to [fd66::55:5]:53 comment "external exit myext: its resolver address, from either hub"
+    iifname { "m06", "m13" } ip saddr 10.66.200.14 meta l4proto tcp dnat ip to 10.66.201.14:12301 comment "external exit myext: TCP to the redirector (SOCKS5 198.51.100.66:1080)"

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian external SOCKS exits health. Managed by Meridian (node manifest).
+# Health = a DNS query over TCP relayed by the redirector through the proxy
+# (TCP reachability through the proxy; no ICMP to the proxy, no credential here).
+set -u
+INTERVAL=10
+TIMEOUT=8
+mkdir -p /run/meridian/ext
+ext_probe() {
+  local addr="$1" port="$2" out
+  # 17-byte query: header (id 0x4d52, RD, one question), root name, NS, IN.
+  out=$(timeout "$TIMEOUT" bash -c 'exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/$0/$1" || exit 1; printf "\x00\x11\x4d\x52\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x01" >&3; head -c 4 <&3' "$addr" "$port" 2>/dev/null | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
+  [ "${out:4:4}" = "4d52" ]
+}
+ext_check() {
+  local id="$1" svc="$2" health="$3" was now
+  was=$(cat "/run/meridian/ext/$id" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
+  if ext_probe "$svc" 5301 || ext_probe "$svc" 5302; then
+    now=up
+    ip addr replace "$health/32" dev lo
+  else
+    now=down
+    ip addr del "$health/32" dev lo 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+  if [ "$now" != "$was" ]; then
+    echo "$now" > "/run/meridian/ext/$id"
+    if [ "$now" = up ]; then
+      echo "meridian-ext-health: $id up (TCP through its proxy answers); health address $health present"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-ext-health: $id down (no TCP answer through its proxy within ${TIMEOUT}s); health address $health removed, the hubs stop using it" >&2
+    fi
+  fi
+}
+ext_all() {
+  ext_check 'myext' 10.66.201.14 10.66.202.14
+  :
+}
+keep_health=' 10.66.202.14 '
+for a in $(ip -o -4 addr show dev lo to 10.66.202.0/24 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $4}'); do case "$keep_health" in *" ${a%%/*} "*) ;; *) ip addr del "$a" dev lo 2>/dev/null || true ;; esac; done

+  ext_all
+  sleep "$INTERVAL"
+done

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-4a5ba470
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m06 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m06 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m13 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m13 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+# rp_filter=2 and no ICMP redirects on Meridian's interfaces only (the
+# managed tunnels, the interface the topology names, mra/mmesh). The kernel
+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the

+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.send_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().

+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.

+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.

+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"

+: > "$raw6"

+  family="$1"; out="$2"

+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi

+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}

+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {

+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}

+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/

+    "family": "ipv4",
+    "raw4": slurp(os.environ["RAW4"]),
+    "raw6": slurp(os.environ["RAW6"]),
+    "ai": slurp(os.environ["AI"]),

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4
+# meridian-ext: myext socks=198.51.100.66:1080 iface=wg9
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf

===== nodes/gb1/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-4e89086b
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m07 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m07 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m14 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m14 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+# Policy routes for one Meridian node. Safe to re-run.
+# fd66::/48 is never given a next hop of the ROS gateway.

+# rp_filter=2 and no ICMP redirects on Meridian's interfaces only (the
+# managed tunnels, the interface the topology names, mra/mmesh). The kernel
+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the
+# interface value is what matters here. Other interfaces are not touched.
+harden_sysctl() {
+  local i
+  for i in "$@"; do
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.rp_filter=2" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.send_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

+#!/bin/bash
+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='gb1'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"
+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"
+run_rc() {
+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/
+probe grok https://grok.x.ai/
+token_file=/etc/meridian/unlock-report.env
+if [ -f "$token_file" ] && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  tok=$(sed -n 's/^MERIDIAN_PANEL_TOKEN=//p' "$token_file" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
+  case "$tok" in
+    ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._~/+-]*)
+      echo "unlock report skipped: token missing or refused" >&2
+      ;;
+    *)
+      body=$(EXIT_ID="$exit_id" STARTED="$started" RAW4="$raw4" RAW6="$raw6" AI="$ai" python3 - <<'PY'
+import json, os
+def slurp(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as fh:
+            return fh.read()[-100000:]
+    except OSError:
+        return ""
+# raw4/raw6 are the -M 4 / -M 6 runs; the AI probes use curl -4.
+print(json.dumps({
+    "exit_id": os.environ["EXIT_ID"],
+    "kind": "scheduled",
+    "at": os.environ["STARTED"],
+    "family": "ipv4",
+    "raw4": slurp(os.environ["RAW4"]),
+    "raw6": slurp(os.environ["RAW6"]),
+    "ai": slurp(os.environ["AI"]),
+}))
+PY
+)
+      hdr=$(mktemp)
+      chmod 600 "$hdr"
+      printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$tok" > "$hdr"
+      curl --silent --show-error --max-time 20 --config "$hdr" \
+        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+        --data-binary "$body" \
+        "$panel/api/unlock/report" >/dev/null || true
+      rm -f "$hdr"
+      ;;
+  esac
+fi
+echo "unlock-probe-wrote $raw"
