+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+# The MTU each tunnel interface's config sets ("MTU ="): wg syncconf keeps the
+# running interface MTU, so an existing interface is aligned in place below.
+wg_conf_mtu() {
+  case "$1" in
+    m07) echo 1420 ;;
+    m14) echo 1420 ;;
+    *) echo "" ;;
+  esac
+}
+for iface in m07 m14; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+    want_mtu=$(wg_conf_mtu "$iface")
+    have_mtu=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$iface/mtu" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [ -n "$want_mtu" ] && [ "$have_mtu" != "$want_mtu" ]; then
+      ip link set dev "$iface" mtu "$want_mtu"
+      echo "meridian-wg-mtu: $iface ${have_mtu:-?} -> $want_mtu (set in place; the tunnel stays up)"
+    fi
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+if [ -e /lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ] || [ -e /usr/lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ]; then
+  nd=/etc/systemd/networkd.conf.d/90-meridian.conf
+  nd_want='# meridian: keep Meridian ip rules and routes when systemd-networkd restarts
+[Network]
+ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=no
+ManageForeignRoutes=no'
+  if [ "$(cat "$nd" 2>/dev/null)" != "$nd_want" ]; then
+    if mkdir -p "${nd%/*}" && printf '%s\n' "$nd_want" > "$nd.tmp" && chmod 0644 "$nd.tmp" && mv -f "$nd.tmp" "$nd"; then
+      echo "meridian-networkd: wrote $nd (networkd not restarted; it applies at its next start)"
+    else
+      rm -f "$nd.tmp"
+      echo "meridian-networkd: could not write $nd; a networkd restart would delete the Meridian ip rules" >&2
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit meridian-unlock.timer
+if [ -f /etc/smartdns/smartdns.conf ] && [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  if systemctl cat meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    systemctl enable meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    systemctl restart meridian-smartdns.service || echo "meridian-smartdns.service restart failed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  else
+    echo "meridian-smartdns.service is not installed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  fi
+fi
+echo meridian-up-complete

+#!/usr/sbin/nft -f
+# Meridian early-boot LAN guard. Loaded by meridian-guard.service before
+# forwarding can be enabled. Replaces only table inet meridian_guard.
+# LAN fail-closed guard. Independent of table inet meridian: it reads only
+# the fwmark and the output interface, so if classification is missing
+# every forwarded LAN packet is unmarked and dropped here.
+table inet meridian_guard
+delete table inet meridian_guard
+table inet meridian_guard {
+  chain forward {
+    type filter hook forward priority -200; policy accept;
+    iifname "eth0" meta l4proto { tcp, udp } th dport { 53, 853 } drop comment "DNS is answered locally, never forwarded"
+    iifname "eth0" meta mark 0x64 oifname "eth0" return comment "domestic: direct via ROS or LAN only"
+    iifname "eth0" meta mark 0x101-0x140 oifname { "m02", "m02w", "m03", "m04" } return comment "exit marks: WireGuard only"
+    iifname "eth0" meta mark 0x65 meta l4proto tcp reject with tcp reset comment "reject rules: TCP reset"
+    iifname "eth0" meta mark 0x65 reject with icmpx port-unreachable comment "reject rules: ICMP port unreachable"
+    iifname "eth0" counter drop comment "fail closed: unclassified or misrouted LAN traffic, v4 and v6"
+  }
+}

+# Meridian SmartDNS. Real answers, no fake-ip.
+# ECS is intentionally unset so the family prefix is not attached to queries.
+# Queries to an exit resolver leave from that exit's WAN, so DNS and the data path share a region.
+# A region group the hub switches resolves through its own data path (group mark, group
+# resolver address), so its DNS always reaches the member the hub currently uses.
+speed-check-mode none
+dualstack-ip-selection no
+cache-size 65536
+cache-persist no
+serve-expired yes
+rr-ttl-min 60
+bind [::]:53
+bind-tcp [::]:53
+# DoT certificate will not match the name the client dialed. Strict clients fail closed and fall back to port 53.
+# The certificate is global in SmartDNS (bind-cert-*); bind-tls takes no certificate options.
+bind-cert-file /etc/meridian/dns/cert.pem
+bind-cert-key-file /etc/meridian/dns/key.pem
+bind-tls [::]:853
+
+# AAAA: clients take IPv6 from the home router, not from this gateway (settings
+# clients_ipv6_via_gateway off): IPv6 to a tunnelled name would leave over the home line.
+# No AAAA (empty NOERROR, IPv6 hints dropped from HTTPS records) for any name except the
+# domestic sets and the rules allowed IPv6, which carry "-address -6".
+force-AAAA-SOA yes
+
+server-tls 192.0.2.53:853 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
+server 192.0.2.53 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
+server-tls 198.51.100.53:853 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
+server 198.51.100.53 -group domestic -exclude-default-group
+
+server fd66::54:1 -group g_dc1 -exclude-default-group
+server fd66::54:2 -group g_dc2 -exclude-default-group
+server fd66::54:3 -group g_gb1 -exclude-default-group
+server fd66::54:4 -group g_jp_a -exclude-default-group
+server fd66::54:5 -group g_myext -exclude-default-group
+server fd66::54:6 -group g_sg1 -exclude-default-group
+server fd66::54:7 -group g_twnat -exclude-default-group
+server fd66::54:8 -group g_us1 -exclude-default-group
+server fd66::54:9 -group g_us2 -exclude-default-group
+
+# region groups switched by the hub: the group's resolver address, the group mark on the socket
+server fd66::53:a -group rg_gb -exclude-default-group -set-mark 266
+server fd66::53:b -group rg_hk -set-mark 267
+server fd66::53:c -group rg_jp -exclude-default-group -set-mark 268
+server fd66::53:d -group rg_my -exclude-default-group -set-mark 269
+server fd66::53:e -group rg_sg -exclude-default-group -set-mark 270
+server fd66::53:f -group rg_tw -exclude-default-group -set-mark 271

+#!/bin/bash
+# Relay sharing: every relay carries new connections at the weight the controller
+# (meridian path-step: measure, decide, record) sets from measured path quality; the
+# backup hub only while every relay is persistently below the usable floor.
+# Fallback when path-step is unavailable: equal weights over the relays that answer,
+# reachability only. Nothing answering: tables stay on tunnels (never the LAN NIC).
+set -u
+# relay sharing (compile.planShare); only share_apply changes the map and the relay tables at run time
+SH_NAME=('access' 'access2')
+SH_LEGS=('m02 m02w' 'm03')
+SH_PROBE=('10.66.1.2' '10.66.2.2')
+SH_TABLE=(111 112)
+SH_VALUE=(0x00010000 0x00020000)
+SH_BK_HUB='hkb'
+SH_BK_IFACE='m04'
+SH_BK_PROBE='10.66.5.2'
+SH_BK_TABLE='109'
+SH_BK_VALUE='0x00fe0000'
+SH_PRIMARY='ix'
+SH_IN='"eth0"'
+SH_HASH4='jhash ip saddr . ip daddr . th sport . th dport mod 1000 seed 0x4d52'
+SH_HASH6='jhash ip6 saddr . ip6 daddr . th sport . th dport mod 1000 seed 0x4d52'
+UP_STATE=/run/meridian/upstream
+SH_APPLIED=/run/meridian/pathq/applied
+SH_VERSION=cce66594bb535bd02e8ca5d98c124f79c855436f9d3a834999d38294105ecd96
+
+SH_TXN="${SH_APPLIED%/*}/switch"
+share_lock() {
+  mkdir -p "$SH_TXN" || return 4
+  chmod 700 "$SH_TXN" || return 4
+  exec 8>>"$SH_TXN/lock" || return 4
+  flock -w 30 8 || return 4
+}
+share_guard_on() {
+  # Independent table: neither the assignment batch nor installation of the
+  # base rules can remove this fence. Existing guards still evaluate returns.
+  nft -f - <<'SH_GUARD'
+table inet meridian_switch
+delete table inet meridian_switch
+table inet meridian_switch {
+  chain forward {
+    type filter hook forward priority -310; policy accept;
+    ip daddr 10.66.0.0/16 tcp dport 22 return
+    ip6 daddr fd66::/48 tcp dport 22 return
+    ip saddr 10.66.0.0/16 tcp sport 22 ct state established return
+    ip6 saddr fd66::/48 tcp sport 22 ct state established return
+    counter drop
+  }
+  chain output {
+    type filter hook output priority -10; policy accept;
+    oifname "lo" return
+    meta mark 0x4d72 return
+    ip daddr 10.66.0.0/16 tcp dport 22 return
+    ip6 daddr fd66::/48 tcp dport 22 return
+    ip daddr 10.66.0.0/16 tcp sport 22 return
+    ip6 daddr fd66::/48 tcp sport 22 return
+    udp dport 53 drop
+    tcp dport 53 drop
+    meta mark & 0x00ff0000 != 0 drop
+    meta mark & 0x0000ffff >= 0x100 meta mark & 0x0000ffff <= 0x1fff drop
+    ip daddr 10.66.0.0/16 drop
+    ip6 daddr fd66::/48 drop
+  }
+}
+SH_GUARD
+}
+share_guard_off() { nft delete table inet meridian_switch; }
+share_atomic_copy() {
+  local src="$1" dst="$2"
+  mkdir -p "${dst%/*}" || return 4
+  cp "$src" "$dst.next" && mv -f "$dst.next" "$dst" || return 4
+}
+share_error() {
+  local code="$1" state="$2" tmp="$UP_STATE.error"
+  echo "meridian-switch: $code; automatic switching blocked until a complete install" >&2
+  # Keep the old carrying decision/times as history; down means not confirmed.
+  if [ -f "$UP_STATE" ]; then
+    sed -e "s/^state .*/state $state/" -e "s/^alert .*/alert $code/" "$UP_STATE" > "$tmp" && mv -f "$tmp" "$UP_STATE" || return 4

+share_restore() {
+  local old="$1" args=()
+  [ -f "$old/version" ] && [ "$(cat "$old/version")" = "$SH_VERSION" ] || return 4
+  read -r -a args < "$old/args" || return 4

+  if [ -f "$old/state" ]; then
+    share_atomic_copy "$old/state" "${PQ_STATE:-${SH_APPLIED%/*}/state.json}" || return 4
+  else
+    rm -f "${PQ_STATE:-${SH_APPLIED%/*}/state.json}" || return 4
+  fi
+}
+share_publish() {
+  # The caller prepared status/state in a private generation directory.
+  share_atomic_copy "$SH_CANDIDATE/status" "$UP_STATE" || return 4
+  if [ -f "$SH_CANDIDATE/state" ]; then
+    share_atomic_copy "$SH_CANDIDATE/state" "${PQ_STATE:-${SH_APPLIED%/*}/state.json}" || return 4
+  else
+    rm -f "${PQ_STATE:-${SH_APPLIED%/*}/state.json}" || return 4
+  fi

+share_apply() {
+  # Direct callers use the same serialization as controller/install callers.
+  if [ "${SH_LOCKED:-0}" != 1 ]; then
+    ( share_lock || exit $?; SH_LOCKED=1; share_apply "$@" )
+    return $?
+  fi
+  local old="" rc=0 recovered=0
+  [ -n "${SH_CANDIDATE:-}" ] && [ -f "$SH_CANDIDATE/status" ] || return 4

+  SH_VALIDATE=1 share_apply_raw "$@" || return $?

+  if [ "${SH_INSTALL:-0}" != 1 ] && { [ -e "$SH_TXN/blocked" ] || [ -e "$SH_TXN/pending" ]; }; then

+    rm -f "$SH_APPLIED"
+    touch "$SH_TXN/blocked"

+  fi

+  # restart fences and blocks instead of taking the partial state as success.
+  printf '%s %s\n' "$SH_VERSION" "${SH_CANDIDATE##*/}" > "$SH_TXN/pending" || return 4
+  rm -f "$SH_APPLIED" || return 4
+  share_guard_on || { touch "$SH_TXN/blocked"; share_error guard_failed down; return 4; }

+  [ "$rc" -ne 1 ] || rc=3

+    printf '%s\n' "${SH_CANDIDATE##*/}" > "$SH_TXN/current.next" && mv -f "$SH_TXN/current.next" "$SH_TXN/current" || rc=4

+  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
+    [ -z "$old" ] || [ "$old" = "$SH_CANDIDATE" ] || rm -rf "$old"
+    return 0
+  fi

+  # fence and latches blocked. Never restore a candidate or the partial site.
+  touch "$SH_TXN/blocked"
+  rm -f "$SH_APPLIED"
+  if share_guard_on && [ -n "$old" ] && share_restore "$old" && share_guard_off; then recovered=1; fi
+  if [ "$recovered" = 1 ]; then
+    # Back on the last successful snapshot, unfenced. Automatic switching is
+    # held: retry after a bounded backoff (30 s, then 60 s), at most
+    # SH_RETRIES failed attempts, then only a complete install clears it.
+    local count=0 next
+    rm -f "$SH_TXN/blocked"

+    printf '%s\n' "${old##*/}" > "$SH_TXN/current.next" && mv -f "$SH_TXN/current.next" "$SH_TXN/current" || touch "$SH_TXN/blocked"

+    share_drop_candidate
+    [ -e "$SH_TXN/blocked" ] || printf '%s\n' "$(cat "$old/args")" > "$SH_APPLIED"

+  else
+    share_guard_on || true
+    # Restore the historical record even when route compensation failed.
+    if [ -n "$old" ]; then share_atomic_copy "$old/status" "$UP_STATE" || true
+    elif [ -f "$SH_CANDIDATE/history" ]; then share_atomic_copy "$SH_CANDIDATE/history" "$UP_STATE" || true; fi

+  fi

+# share_finish_pending: a pending marker left by a killed pass. The commit
+# point is "current" naming the pending target: it is written only after the
+# kernel switch, publication and fence removal all succeeded. When it does,
+# and the snapshot is complete for this compiled version, the kernel state is
+# verified by replaying the snapshot under the fence (the switch's own
+# commands; any failure keeps the fence and blocks). Then the commit finishes
+# without a full install. Anything unprovable stays pending: fenced, blocked.
+share_finish_pending() {
+  local pv pt cur snap args=()
+  read -r pv pt < "$SH_TXN/pending" || return 4
+  [ "$pv" = "$SH_VERSION" ] || return 4
+  case "$pt" in *[!A-Za-z0-9-]*|'') return 4 ;; snapshot-*) ;; *) return 4 ;; esac
+  [ -f "$SH_TXN/current" ] && read -r cur < "$SH_TXN/current" || return 4

+  snap="$SH_TXN/$pt"
+  [ -f "$snap/status" ] && [ -f "$snap/args" ] && [ "$(cat "$snap/version" 2>/dev/null)" = "$SH_VERSION" ] || return 4
+  read -r -a args < "$snap/args" || return 4

+  SH_VALIDATE=1 share_apply_raw "${args[@]}" || return 4
+  share_guard_on || return 4
+  if ! share_apply_raw "${args[@]}"; then touch "$SH_TXN/blocked"; return 4; fi
+  share_guard_off || { touch "$SH_TXN/blocked"; return 4; }
+  printf '%s\n' "${args[*]}" > "$SH_APPLIED.next" && mv -f "$SH_APPLIED.next" "$SH_APPLIED" || return 4
+  rm -f "$SH_TXN/pending"
+}
+SH_RETRIES=3
+# share_held: 0 while a compensated failure holds automatic switching (backoff
+# not over, or the retry budget spent). The last successful path stays applied.
+share_held() {

+  [ -f "$SH_TXN/failed" ] || return 1

+  [ "$count" -ge "$SH_RETRIES" ] || [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$next" ]

+# share_drop_candidate: remove an unpublished candidate (never the current).

+share_candidate() {

+share_index() {

+share_leg_ok() {
+  case "$2" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.-]*) return 1 ;; esac
+  case " ${SH_LEGS[$1]} " in *" $2 "*) return 0 ;; esac
+  return 1
+}
+share_table_route() {
+  ip route replace default dev "$2" table "$1" || return 3
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$1" || return 3
+  ip -6 route replace default dev "$2" table "$1" || return 3
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$1" || return 3
+}
+# share_tables LEG_1 … LEG_n: each relay's table on the given leg; the backup table.
+share_tables() {
+  local i=0 leg
+  for leg in "$@"; do
+    share_leg_ok "$i" "$leg" || { echo "share_tables: $leg is not a leg of ${SH_NAME[$i]}" >&2; return 1; }
+    share_table_route "${SH_TABLE[$i]}" "$leg" || return $?
+    i=$((i + 1))
+  done
+  if [ -n "$SH_BK_IFACE" ]; then share_table_route "$SH_BK_TABLE" "$SH_BK_IFACE" || return $?; fi
+  return 0
+}
+# share_designate IFACE: table 102 and this host's routes to the tunnel prefixes.
+share_designate() {
+  local iface="$1"
+  [ -n "$iface" ] || return 1
+  ip route replace default dev "$iface" table 102 || return 3
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 102 || return 3
+  ip -6 route replace default dev "$iface" table 102 || return 3
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table 102 || return 3
+  ip route replace 10.66.0.0/16 dev "$iface" || return 3
+  ip route replace blackhole 10.66.0.0/16 metric 32767 || return 3
+  ip -6 route replace fd66::/48 dev "$iface" || return 3
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole fd66::/48 metric 32767 || return 3
+}
+# share_map W_1 … W_n: the assignment map (ranges of jhash … mod 1000).
+share_map() {
+  local i=0 lo=0 w parts=""
+  for w in "$@"; do
+    if [ "$w" -gt 0 ]; then
+      parts="${parts:+$parts, }$lo-$((lo + w - 1)) : ${SH_VALUE[$i]}"
+      lo=$((lo + w))
+    fi
+    i=$((i + 1))
+  done
+  [ -n "$parts" ] || parts="0-999 : $SH_BK_VALUE"
+  echo "map { $parts }"
+}
+# share_apply UP DESIGNATED LEG_1 W_1 D_1 … LEG_n W_n D_n BACKUP_DRAIN
+# Checks every value against the compiled arrays (1: refused), then
+# changes the map, the redirect and drain rules in ONE nft batch (refused
+# whole or applied whole; 2: nft refused it, nothing changed), the relay
+# tables and table 102. Nothing else.
+share_apply_raw() {
+  local up="$1" des="$2" n=${#SH_NAME[@]} i sum=0 leg w d bk map desif redirect="" drain="" v
+  shift 2
+  if [ $# -ne $((3 * n + 1)) ]; then echo "share_apply: wrong argument count" >&2; return 1; fi
+  local legs=() ws=() ds=()
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    leg="$1"; w="$2"; d="$3"; shift 3
+    share_leg_ok "$i" "$leg" || { echo "share_apply: $leg is not a leg of ${SH_NAME[$i]}" >&2; return 1; }
+    case "$w" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "share_apply: bad weight" >&2; return 1 ;; esac
+    [ "$w" -le 1000 ] || { echo "share_apply: bad weight" >&2; return 1; }
+    case "$d" in 0|1) ;; *) echo "share_apply: bad drain flag" >&2; return 1 ;; esac
+    legs+=("$leg"); ws+=("$w"); ds+=("$d"); sum=$((sum + w))
+  done
+  bk="$1"
+  case "$bk" in 0|1) ;; *) echo "share_apply: bad backup drain flag" >&2; return 1 ;; esac
+  case "$up" in
+    main)
+      [ "$sum" -eq 1000 ] || { echo "share_apply: weights must sum to 1000" >&2; return 1; }
+      i=$(share_index "$des") || { echo "share_apply: $des is not a relay" >&2; return 1; }
+      desif="${legs[$i]}"
+      ;;
+    backup)
+      [ -n "$SH_BK_IFACE" ] && [ "$sum" -eq 0 ] && [ "$des" = backup ] || { echo "share_apply: bad backup decision" >&2; return 1; }
+      desif="$SH_BK_IFACE"
+      ;;
+    *) echo "share_apply: bad upstream" >&2; return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  [ "${SH_VALIDATE:-0}" != 1 ] || return 0
+  map=$(share_map "${ws[@]}")
+  for ((i = 0; i <= n; i++)); do
+    if [ "$i" -lt "$n" ]; then
+      [ "${ds[$i]}" = 1 ] || continue
+      v="${SH_VALUE[$i]}"
+    else
+      [ "$bk" = 1 ] && [ -n "$SH_BK_IFACE" ] || continue
+      v="$SH_BK_VALUE"
+    fi
+    redirect="${redirect}add rule inet meridian relay_redirect ct mark $v meta l4proto != tcp meta nfproto ipv4 ct mark set $SH_HASH4 $map
+add rule inet meridian relay_redirect ct mark $v meta l4proto != tcp meta nfproto ipv6 ct mark set $SH_HASH6 $map
+"
+    drain="${drain}add rule inet meridian relay_drain iifname $SH_IN ct direction original ct mark $v meta l4proto tcp reject with tcp reset
+"
+  done
+  if ! printf 'flush chain inet meridian relay_assign\nadd rule inet meridian relay_assign meta nfproto ipv4 ct mark set %s %s\nadd rule inet meridian relay_assign meta nfproto ipv6 ct mark set %s %s\nflush chain inet meridian relay_redirect\n%sflush chain inet meridian relay_drain\n%s' \
+    "$SH_HASH4" "$map" "$SH_HASH6" "$map" "$redirect" "$drain" | nft -f -; then
+    echo "share_apply: nft refused the batch; the previous map stays" >&2
+    return 2
+  fi
+  share_tables "${legs[@]}" || return $?
+  share_designate "$desif"
+}
+# share_record STATE CONTROLLER UP DESIGNATED SINCE SWITCHED ALERT: the
+# upstream record from the shell (the install, and the fallback when
+# path-step is unavailable); relay lines from SH_R_* (no measurements).
+share_record() {
+  local state="$1" ctl="$2" up="$3" des="$4" since="$5" sw="$6" alert="$7" i tmp iface hub tier
+  if [ "$up" = backup ]; then
+    iface="$SH_BK_IFACE"; hub="$SH_BK_HUB"; tier=backup
+  else
+    i=$(share_index "$des") || i=0
+    iface="${SH_R_LEG[$i]}"; hub="$SH_PRIMARY"; tier=primary
+  fi
+  mkdir -p "${UP_STATE%/*}" || return 4
+  tmp="${UP_STATE%/*}/.upstream.$$"
+  {
+    echo "meridian-upstream 2"
+    echo "beat $(date +%s)"
+    echo "path $up"
+    echo "iface $iface"
+    echo "hub $hub"
+    echo "tier $tier"
+    echo "since $since"
+    echo "state $state"
+    echo "controller $ctl"
+    echo "alert $alert"
+    echo "switched $sw"
+    echo "designated $des"
+    for ((i = 0; i < ${#SH_NAME[@]}; i++)); do
+      echo "relay ${SH_NAME[$i]} ${SH_R_LEG[$i]} ${SH_R_STATUS[$i]} ${SH_R_W[$i]} 0 ${SH_R_REASON[$i]} $since ${SH_R_GRADE[$i]} - - - - 0 0 0 0 0 0 - 0 - - - 0 ${SH_R_QOS[$i]:-$SH_QOS_DEF} ${SH_R_SPEED[$i]:--} ${SH_R_SPAT[$i]:-0} ${SH_R_BASE[$i]:-0} ${SH_R_BSRC[$i]:--}"
+    done
+    if [ -n "$SH_BK_IFACE" ]; then echo "backup $SH_BK_HUB $SH_BK_IFACE ${SH_BK_GRADE:-none} - - - - 0 0 0 0"; fi
+    echo "end"
+  } > "$tmp" && mv -f "$tmp" "$UP_STATE" || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 4; }
+  return 0
+}
+SH_QOS_ON=1
+SH_QOS_DEF=unknown
+QOS_FILE=/var/lib/meridian-pathq/qos
+QOS_MAX_AGE=604800
+SH_R_LEG=(m02 m03)
+SH_R_W=(500 500)
+SH_R_STATUS=(active active)
+SH_R_GRADE=(none none)
+SH_R_REASON=(- -)
+MERIDIAN_BIN=/usr/local/bin/meridian
+PQ_CONFIG=/etc/meridian/path-quality.json
+PQ_STATE=/run/meridian/pathq/state.json
+INTERVAL=5
+FAILS_NEED=3
+RECOVERS_NEED=5
+COOLDOWN=120
+fb_up=main
+fb_des='access'
+fb_since=$(date +%s)
+fb_switched=0
+fb_fails=(0 0)
+fb_goods=(0 0)
+fb_in=(1 1)
+SH_BK_GRADE=none
+share_alive() {
+  ping -n -q -I "$1" -c 1 -W 2 "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1
+}
+# share_decide TEXT: 0 applied (or unchanged), 1 refused (use the
+# fallback), 2 valid but not applied (logged; the previous state stays).
+share_decide() {
+  local text="$1" up="" des="" bk="" n=${#SH_NAME[@]} i=0 args=() f first=1
+  while read -r -a f; do
+    if [ "$first" = 1 ]; then
+      [ "${f[*]:-}" = "meridian-pathq 1" ] || return 1
+      first=0
+      continue
+    fi
+    case "${f[0]:-}" in
+      upstream) up="${f[1]:-}" ;;
+      designated) des="${f[1]:-}" ;;
+      relay)
+        [ "$i" -lt "$n" ] && [ "${f[1]:-}" = "${SH_NAME[$i]}" ] && [ "${#f[@]}" -eq 5 ] || return 1
+        args+=("${f[2]}" "${f[3]}" "${f[4]}")
+        i=$((i + 1))
+        ;;
+      backup) bk="${f[1]:-}" ;;
+      end) ;;
+      *) return 1 ;;
+    esac
+  done <<< "$text"
+  [ "$first" = 0 ] && [ "$i" -eq "$n" ] && [ -n "$up" ] && [ -n "$des" ] && [ -n "$bk" ] || return 1
+  share_once "$up $des ${args[*]} $bk" "$up" "$des" "${args[@]}" "$bk" || return $?
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    SH_R_LEG[$i]="${args[$((3 * i))]}"
+    SH_R_W[$i]="${args[$((3 * i + 1))]}"
+  done
+  share_load_applied
+  return $?
+}
+share_fallback_candidate() {
+  local n=${#SH_NAME[@]} i l alive now cnt=0 bk_alive=0 up des state=ok w args=() share rest first=-1
+  now=$(date +%s)
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    alive=""
+    for l in ${SH_LEGS[$i]}; do
+      if share_alive "$l" "${SH_PROBE[$i]}"; then alive="$l"; break; fi
+    done
+    if [ -n "$alive" ]; then
+      SH_R_LEG[$i]="$alive"; SH_R_GRADE[$i]=good; fb_fails[$i]=0
+      if [ "${fb_in[$i]}" = 0 ]; then
+        fb_goods[$i]=$((fb_goods[$i] + 1))
+        if [ "${fb_goods[$i]}" -ge "$RECOVERS_NEED" ]; then fb_in[$i]=1; fb_goods[$i]=0; fi
+      fi
+    else
+      SH_R_GRADE[$i]=down; fb_goods[$i]=0
+      if [ "${fb_in[$i]}" = 1 ]; then
+        fb_fails[$i]=$((fb_fails[$i] + 1))
+        if [ "${fb_fails[$i]}" -ge "$FAILS_NEED" ]; then fb_in[$i]=0; fb_fails[$i]=0; fi
+      fi
+    fi
+    if [ "${fb_in[$i]}" = 1 ]; then cnt=$((cnt + 1)); SH_R_STATUS[$i]=active; SH_R_REASON[$i]=-; else SH_R_STATUS[$i]=evicted; SH_R_REASON[$i]=down; fi
+  done
+  # The speed tests' saved verdict decides which of the reachable relays
+  # carry (share_qos_select); throttling never decides the backup hub.
+  share_qos_read
+  SH_BK_GRADE=none
+  if [ -n "$SH_BK_IFACE" ]; then
+    if share_alive "$SH_BK_IFACE" "$SH_BK_PROBE"; then bk_alive=1; SH_BK_GRADE=good; else SH_BK_GRADE=down; fi
+  fi
+  up="$fb_up"
+  if [ "$up" = main ] && [ "$cnt" -eq 0 ] && [ "$bk_alive" = 1 ]; then
+    up=backup
+  elif [ "$up" = backup ] && [ "$cnt" -gt 0 ] && { [ "$fb_switched" -eq 0 ] || [ $((now - fb_switched)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" ]; }; then
+    up=main
+  fi
+  if [ "$up" != "$fb_up" ]; then fb_switched=$now; fb_since=$now; fi
+  fb_up="$up"
+  # Equal weights over the relays in; none in: equal over all (the traffic
+  # is dropped in the tunnels either way).
+  local sel=() m=0
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    sel[$i]="${fb_in[$i]}"
+  done
+  share_qos_select
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    [ "${sel[$i]}" = 1 ] && m=$((m + 1))
+  done
+  if [ "$m" -eq 0 ]; then
+    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do sel[$i]=1; done
+    m=$n
+  fi
+  share=$((1000 / m)); rest=$((1000 - share * m))
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    if [ "${sel[$i]}" = 1 ]; then
+      SH_R_W[$i]=$((share + rest)); rest=0
+      [ "$first" -ge 0 ] || first=$i
+    else
+      SH_R_W[$i]=0
+    fi
+  done
+  fb_des="${SH_NAME[$first]}"
+  des="$fb_des"
+  if [ "$up" = backup ]; then
+    des=backup
+    [ "$bk_alive" = 1 ] || state=down
+  elif [ "$cnt" -eq 0 ]; then
+    state=down
+  fi
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    w="${SH_R_W[$i]}"
+    [ "$up" = backup ] && w=0
+    args+=("${SH_R_LEG[$i]}" "$w" 0)
+  done
+  share_candidate || return 4
+  ( UP_STATE="$SH_CANDIDATE/status"; share_record "$state" shell "$up" "$des" "$fb_since" "$fb_switched" controller_unavailable ) || return 4
+  share_once "$up $des ${args[*]} 0" "$up" "$des" "${args[@]}" 0 || return $?
+
+}
+# share_qos_read: the speed tests' verdict file into SH_R_QOS/SPEED/SPAT/
+# BASE/BSRC and QOS_T (1: throttled and fresh). The same grammar as
+# pathquality.ParseQoS: any deviation ignores the whole file (no relay is
+# then throttled). Only the file is read; nothing is measured or inferred.
+share_qos_read() {
+  local n=${#SH_NAME[@]} i v line now done=0 f
+  local tq=() ts=() tk=() ta=() tb=() tr=()
+  SH_R_QOS=(); SH_R_SPEED=(); SH_R_SPAT=(); SH_R_BASE=(); SH_R_BSRC=(); QOS_T=()
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do SH_R_QOS[$i]=$SH_QOS_DEF; SH_R_SPEED[$i]=-; SH_R_SPAT[$i]=0; SH_R_BASE[$i]=0; SH_R_BSRC[$i]=-; QOS_T[$i]=0; done
+  [ "$SH_QOS_ON" = 1 ] && [ -f "$QOS_FILE" ] || return 0
+  i=-1
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    if [ "$i" -lt 0 ]; then [ "$line" = "meridian-qos 1" ] || return 0; i=0; continue; fi
+    if [ "$line" = end ]; then [ "$i" -eq "$n" ] && done=1; break; fi
+    read -r -a f <<< "$line"
+    [ "$i" -lt "$n" ] && [ "${#f[@]}" -eq 8 ] && [ "${f[0]}" = relay ] && [ "${f[1]}" = "${SH_NAME[$i]}" ] || return 0
+    case "${f[2]}" in ok|throttled|unknown) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
+    case "${f[7]}" in nominal|p90) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
+    for v in "${f[3]}" "${f[5]}" "${f[6]}"; do case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 0 ;; esac; done
+    case "${f[4]}" in -) ;; ''|*[!0-9]*) return 0 ;; esac
+    tq[$i]="${f[2]}"; tk[$i]="${f[4]}"; ta[$i]="${f[5]}"; tb[$i]="${f[6]}"; tr[$i]="${f[7]}"
+    i=$((i + 1))
+  done < "$QOS_FILE"
+  [ "$done" = 1 ] || return 0
+  now=$(date +%s)
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    SH_R_QOS[$i]="${tq[$i]}"; SH_R_SPEED[$i]="${tk[$i]}"; SH_R_SPAT[$i]="${ta[$i]}"; SH_R_BASE[$i]="${tb[$i]}"; SH_R_BSRC[$i]="${tr[$i]}"
+    if [ "${tq[$i]}" = throttled ]; then
+      if [ "${ta[$i]}" -gt 0 ] && [ $((now - ta[$i])) -le "$QOS_MAX_AGE" ]; then QOS_T[$i]=1; else SH_R_QOS[$i]=unknown; fi
+    fi
+  done
+}
+# share_qos_select: among the selected (reachable) relays, the throttled
+# ones carry nothing while another carries; when all of them are throttled
+# only the one with the best last test carries (ties: the first).
+share_qos_select() {
+  local n=${#SH_NAME[@]} i k=0 best=-1 bk=-1 sp
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    [ "${sel[$i]}" = 1 ] || continue
+    if [ "${QOS_T[$i]:-0}" = 0 ]; then k=$((k + 1)); fi
+  done
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    [ "${sel[$i]}" = 1 ] && [ "${QOS_T[$i]:-0}" = 1 ] || continue
+    sp="${SH_R_SPEED[$i]}"; [ "$sp" != - ] || sp=0
+    if [ "$k" -eq 0 ] && [ "$sp" -gt "$bk" ]; then best=$i; bk=$sp; fi
+  done
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    [ "${sel[$i]}" = 1 ] && [ "${QOS_T[$i]:-0}" = 1 ] || continue
+    if [ "$i" = "$best" ]; then
+      SH_R_STATUS[$i]=reduced; SH_R_REASON[$i]=retained_best
+    else
+      sel[$i]=0; SH_R_STATUS[$i]=reduced; SH_R_REASON[$i]=qos_throttled
+    fi
+  done
+}
+# share_speedtest_kick: one background run of the speed tests (at most one
+# test per run, under the controller's lock; nothing due: it exits at once).
+share_speedtest_kick() {
+  [ "$SH_QOS_ON" = 1 ] || return 0
+  ( MERIDIAN_BIND=- timeout 120 "$MERIDIAN_BIN" path-speedtest --config "$PQ_CONFIG" --state "$PQ_STATE" >/dev/null 2>&1 & )
+}
+share_fallback_step() {
+  # A failed switch changes no fallback state: carrying decision, times and
+  # the eviction/recovery counters all return to their values before it.
+  local s_up="$fb_up" s_des="$fb_des" s_since="$fb_since" s_sw="$fb_switched"
+  local s_in=("${fb_in[@]}") s_goods=("${fb_goods[@]}") s_fails=("${fb_fails[@]}")
+  local s_leg=("${SH_R_LEG[@]}") s_w=("${SH_R_W[@]}") s_st=("${SH_R_STATUS[@]}") s_re=("${SH_R_REASON[@]}") s_gr=("${SH_R_GRADE[@]}")
+  share_fallback_candidate
+  local rc=$?
+  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then read -r SH_LOADED < "$SH_TXN/current" || return 4; return 0; fi
+  fb_up="$s_up"; fb_des="$s_des"; fb_since="$s_since"; fb_switched="$s_sw"
+  fb_in=("${s_in[@]}"); fb_goods=("${s_goods[@]}"); fb_fails=("${s_fails[@]}")
+  SH_R_LEG=("${s_leg[@]}"); SH_R_W=("${s_w[@]}"); SH_R_STATUS=("${s_st[@]}"); SH_R_REASON=("${s_re[@]}"); SH_R_GRADE=("${s_gr[@]}")
+  return "$rc"
+}
+share_load_applied() {
+  local generation key value rest i prev="$fb_up"
+  [ -f "$SH_TXN/current" ] || return 0
+  read -r generation < "$SH_TXN/current" || return 4
+  case "$generation" in *[!A-Za-z0-9-]*|'') return 4 ;; snapshot-*) ;; *) return 4 ;; esac
+  [ "${SH_LOADED:-}" != "$generation" ] || return 0
+  [ "$(cat "$SH_TXN/$generation/version")" = "$SH_VERSION" ] || return 4
+  while read -r key value rest; do
+    case "$key" in
+      path) fb_up="$value" ;;
+      designated) fb_des="$value" ;;
+      since) fb_since="$value" ;;
+      switched) fb_switched="$value" ;;
+      relay)
+        i=$(share_index "$value") || return 4
+        read -r "SH_R_LEG[$i]" "SH_R_STATUS[$i]" "SH_R_W[$i]" rest <<< "$rest"
+        # Only the carrying group's membership is known from an applied
+        # record; other relays keep the fallback's own liveness history.
+        if [ main = "$fb_up" ]; then
+          fb_fails[$i]=0; fb_goods[$i]=0; fb_in[$i]=0
+          [ "${SH_R_W[$i]}" -eq 0 ] || fb_in[$i]=1
+        elif [ "$fb_up" = backup ]; then
+          fb_fails[$i]=0; fb_goods[$i]=0; fb_in[$i]=0
+        fi
+        ;;
+    esac
+  done < "$SH_TXN/$generation/status"
+  if [ "$prev" != "$fb_up" ]; then
+    for ((i = 0; i < ${#SH_NAME[@]}; i++)); do fb_fails[$i]=0; fb_goods[$i]=0; done
+  fi
+  SH_LOADED="$generation"
+}
+share_step_locked() {
+  local out rc extra=()
+  [ ! -e "$SH_TXN/pending" ] || [ -e "$SH_TXN/blocked" ] || share_finish_pending || true
+  if [ -e "$SH_TXN/blocked" ] || [ -e "$SH_TXN/pending" ]; then
+    share_guard_on || return 4
+    rm -f "$SH_APPLIED"
+    touch "$SH_TXN/blocked"
+    share_error recovery_blocked down
+    return 4
+  fi
+  share_load_applied || { share_guard_on; rm -f "$SH_APPLIED"; touch "$SH_TXN/blocked"; share_error config_changed down; return 4; }
+  # Compensated failure: hold the last successful path, no new mutation.
+  if share_held; then return 5; fi
+  [ -z "${PQ_NOW:-}" ] || extra=(--now "$PQ_NOW")
+  share_candidate || return 4
+  if out=$(MERIDIAN_BIND=- timeout 25 "$MERIDIAN_BIN" path-step --config "$PQ_CONFIG" --state "$PQ_STATE" --status "$UP_STATE" --candidate "$SH_CANDIDATE" ${extra[@]+"${extra[@]}"}); then
+    share_decide "$out"
+    rc=$?
+    [ "$rc" -eq 1 ] || { share_drop_candidate; return "$rc"; }
+    echo "path-step decision refused; this pass uses the fallback" >&2
+  fi
+  rm -rf "$SH_CANDIDATE"
+  share_fallback_step
+}
+share_step() {
+  share_lock || return $?
+  local SH_LOCKED=1 rc
+  share_step_locked; rc=$?
+  flock -u 8
+  exec 8>&-
+  return "$rc"
+}
+# --- main loop ---
+mkdir -p "${SH_APPLIED%/*}"
+SH_PASS=0
+# Self-heal: rule priority 17000 is the first one meridian-routes.sh adds.
+RULE_SENTINEL=17000
+rule_missing=0
+rule_heal() {
+  local rules
+  rules=$(ip rule show 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  if printf '%s\n' "$rules" | grep -q "^$RULE_SENTINEL:"; then rule_missing=0; return 0; fi
+  rule_missing=$((rule_missing + 1))
+  [ "$rule_missing" -ge 2 ] || return 0
+  if /usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-rule-heal: policy rule $RULE_SENTINEL was missing; re-ran meridian-routes.sh, restarting the failover loop" >&2
+    exec "$0"
+  fi
+  if [ "$rule_missing" -eq 2 ]; then echo "meridian-rule-heal: policy rule $RULE_SENTINEL is missing and meridian-routes.sh failed; retrying every 5 s" >&2; fi
+  return 0
+}
+while true; do
+  rule_heal
+  share_step
+  SH_PASS=$((SH_PASS + 1))
+  if [ $((SH_PASS % 12)) -eq 1 ]; then share_speedtest_kick; fi
+  sleep "$INTERVAL"
+done

+# set_has_elements FILE SET: the listed nft set has an elements line.
+set_has_elements() {
+  local in=0 l re="^[[:space:]]*set $2 [{]\$" end='^[[:space:]]*[}]$'
+  while IFS= read -r l; do
+    if [ "$in" = 0 ]; then
+      [[ $l =~ $re ]] && in=1
+      continue
+    fi
+    case "$l" in *"elements = {"*) return 0 ;; esac
+    [[ $l =~ $end ]] && return 1
+  done < "$1"
+  return 1
+}
+# guard_block FILE: the text of table inet meridian_guard in an nft file.
+guard_block() {
+  local in=0 l
+  while IFS= read -r l; do
+    [ "$l" = "table inet meridian_guard {" ] && in=1
+    if [ "$in" = 1 ]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$l"
+      [ "$l" = "}" ] && return 0
+    fi
+  done < "$1"
+  return 1
+}
+# ip6_hex ADDR: the 32 hex digits of a plain IPv6 address (lower case, no
+# embedded IPv4); fails on anything else.
+ip6_hex() {
+  local a=$1 head tail g hex="" n i
+  local -a H=() T=()
+  case "$a" in ""|*[!0-9a-f:]*|*::*::*) return 1 ;; esac
+  case "$a" in
+    *::*)
+      head=${a%%::*} tail=${a#*::}
+      [ -z "$head" ] || IFS=: read -r -a H <<< "$head"
+      [ -z "$tail" ] || IFS=: read -r -a T <<< "$tail"
+      n=$((8 - ${#H[@]} - ${#T[@]}))
+      [ "$n" -ge 1 ] || return 1 ;;
+    *)
+      IFS=: read -r -a H <<< "$a"
+      n=0
+      [ "${#H[@]}" = 8 ] || return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  for g in ${H[@]+"${H[@]}"}; do
+    [ -n "$g" ] && [ ${#g} -le 4 ] || return 1
+    hex="$hex$(printf '%04x' "0x$g")"
+  done
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do hex="${hex}0000"; done
+  for g in ${T[@]+"${T[@]}"}; do
+    [ -n "$g" ] && [ ${#g} -le 4 ] || return 1
+    hex="$hex$(printf '%04x' "0x$g")"
+  done
+  printf '%s\n' "$hex"
+}
+# in_lan6_ula DST: DST (an address or prefix, as ip -6 route prints it) lies
+# inside the ULA LAN prefix. Always false when the LAN prefix is not a ULA.
+in_lan6_ula() {
+  local addr=${1%%/*} len=128 hex n r
+  [ -n "$lan6_ula" ] || return 1
+  case "$1" in */*) len=${1#*/} ;; esac
+  case "$len" in ""|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
+  [ "$len" -ge "$lan6_ula_bits" ] || return 1
+  hex=$(ip6_hex "$addr") || return 1
+  n=$((lan6_ula_bits / 4)) r=$((lan6_ula_bits % 4))
+  [ "${hex:0:n}" = "${lan6_ula_hex:0:n}" ] || return 1
+  [ "$r" = 0 ] && return 0
+  [ $((0x${hex:n:1} >> (4 - r))) = $((0x${lan6_ula_hex:n:1} >> (4 - r))) ]
+}
+# route_probe NAME DEV ARGS...: "ip ARGS" (a route lookup) with its raw
+# output kept as NAME.txt; succeeds only when the kernel resolved it to a
+# unicast route leaving on DEV. Otherwise probe_why says what it answered.
+route_probe() {
+  local first re=" dev $2( |\$)"
+  probe_why=""
+  run "$1" ip "${@:3}"
+  IFS= read -r first < "$evdir/$1.txt"
+  if [ "$rc" != 0 ]; then
+    case "$first" in
+      *"cross-device"*) probe_why="$first (source validation failed: a policy rule makes the kernel's reverse lookup fail)" ;;
+      exit=*) probe_why="ip exited $rc without output" ;;
+      *) probe_why="$first (ip exited $rc)" ;;
+    esac
+    return 1
+  fi
+  case "$first" in
+    exit=*) probe_why="no output" ;;
+    unreachable*|blackhole*|prohibit*|throw*|local*) probe_why="$first" ;;
+    *) [[ $first =~ $re ]] || probe_why="$first (not via $2)" ;;
+  esac
+  [ -z "$probe_why" ]
+}
+# probe_check ID WHAT DEV ARGS...: one route probe as a PASS or FAIL.
+probe_check() {
+  local id=$1 what=$2 dev=$3 n="rtget-$1"; shift 3
+  if route_probe "$n" "$dev" "$@"; then
+    pass "$id" "$what resolves out of $dev (ip $*)"
+  else
+    fail "$id" "$what: ip $* answered: $probe_why (evidence $n.txt)"
+  fi
+}
+# probe_tunnels ID WHAT DEV FAMILY DST SRC: a reply from every gateway tunnel
+# interface to DST must leave on DEV.
+probe_tunnels() {
+  local id=$1 what=$2 dev=$3 fam=$4 dst=$5 src=$6 tun bad="" n
+  for tun in $tun_ifaces; do
+    n="rtget-$id-$tun"
+    route_probe "$n" "$dev" "$fam" route get "$dst" from "$src" iif "$tun" || bad="$bad $tun: $probe_why (evidence $n.txt);"
+  done
+  if [ -z "$bad" ]; then
+    pass "$id" "$what from each tunnel ($tun_ifaces) resolves out of $dev"
+  else
+    fail "$id" "$what does not resolve out of $dev for:$bad"
+  fi
+}
+# out_of FILE: the command output without the exit= line run appends.
+out_of() { grep -v '^exit=[0-9]*$' "$1"; }
+# run NAME CMD...: raw output to $evdir/NAME.txt, exit status kept.
+run() {
+  name=$1; shift
+  "$@" > "$evdir/$name.txt" 2>&1
+  rc=$?
+  echo "exit=$rc" >> "$evdir/$name.txt"
+  return $rc
+}
+emit "meridian-verify $ts iface=$iface gateway=$gw_addr ros=$ros4 ros6=${ros6:-unset}"
+
+# --- kernel settings -------------------------------------------------------
+if ! command -v sysctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  unknown sysctl "sysctl not found; no kernel setting was checked (run this on the gateway)"
+else
+  for kv in \
+    net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=2 \
+    net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter=2 \
+    "net.ipv4.conf.$iface.rp_filter=2" \
+    net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects=0 \
+    "net.ipv4.conf.$iface.send_redirects=0" \
+    net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects=0 \
+    net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects=0 \
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 \
+    net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1
+  do
+    key=${kv%=*}; want=${kv##*=}
+    if got=$(sysctl -n "$key" 2>/dev/null); then
+      echo "$key=$got" >> "$evdir/sysctl.txt"
+      if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
+        pass "sysctl $key" "$got"
+      else
+        fail "sysctl $key" "$got, want $want"
+      fi
+    else
+      echo "$key=<unreadable>" >> "$evdir/sysctl.txt"
+      fail "sysctl $key" "not readable"
+    fi
+  done
+fi
+
+# --- addresses and routes --------------------------------------------------
+if ! command -v ip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  unknown routes "ip not found; address, neighbour and ULA route checks not run"
+else
+  if run ip-addr ip -4 -o addr show dev "$iface" && grep -qF " $gw_addr/" "$evdir/ip-addr.txt"; then
+    pass gateway_address "$gw_addr is on $iface"
+  else
+    fail gateway_address "$gw_addr is not on $iface (evidence ip-addr.txt)"
+  fi
+  if run ros-route ip -4 route get "$ros4" && grep -qE " dev $iface( |\$)" "$evdir/ros-route.txt" && ! grep -q " via " "$evdir/ros-route.txt"; then
+    pass ros_neighbour "$ros4 is reached on-link via $iface"
+  else
+    fail ros_neighbour "$ros4 is not an on-link neighbour on $iface (evidence ros-route.txt)"
+  fi
+  if run ip6-routes ip -6 route show table all; then
+    grep -E '^((unreachable|blackhole|prohibit|throw|local|anycast) )?f[cd][0-9a-f]{0,2}:' "$evdir/ip6-routes.txt" > "$evdir/ula-routes.txt" || true
+    # A ULA LAN prefix is on-link on $iface by design (its addresses and
+    # routes go to ula-routes-lan.txt); every other ULA route must not use
+    # $iface. No ULA route at all, the LAN prefix included, may point at ROS.
+    : > "$evdir/ula-routes-lan.txt"
+    : > "$evdir/ula-routes-other.txt"
+    while IFS= read -r l; do
+      d=$l
+      case "$d" in unreachable\ *|blackhole\ *|prohibit\ *|throw\ *|local\ *|anycast\ *) d=${d#* } ;; esac
+      d=${d%% *}
+      if in_lan6_ula "$d"; then
+        printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$evdir/ula-routes-lan.txt"
+      else
+        printf '%s\n' "$l" >> "$evdir/ula-routes-other.txt"
+      fi
+    done < "$evdir/ula-routes.txt"
+    bad=""
+    if grep -qE " dev $iface( |\$)" "$evdir/ula-routes-other.txt"; then bad="leaves via $iface"; fi
+    if [ -n "$ros6" ] && grep -qF "via $ros6 " "$evdir/ula-routes.txt"; then bad="points at ROS $ros6"; fi
+    if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
+      fail ula_not_via_ros "a ULA route $bad (evidence ula-routes.txt)"
+    else
+      if [ -n "$lan6_ula" ]; then
+        pass ula_not_via_ros "no ULA route in any table points at ROS, and none outside the LAN prefix $lan6_ula uses $iface (evidence ula-routes.txt ula-routes-lan.txt)"
+      else
+        pass ula_not_via_ros "no ULA route in any table uses $iface or ROS (evidence ula-routes.txt)"
+      fi
+    fi
+  else
+    fail ula_not_via_ros "ip -6 route show table all failed (evidence ip6-routes.txt)"
+  fi
+
+  # Policy rules as loaded: every compiled exit and region-group mark goes to
+  # the foreign table (102), with an unreachable rule right behind it, v4
+  # and v6. Table 102 may be listed by its name meridian_foreign.
+  rules_ok=1
+  run ip-rules4 ip -4 rule show || rules_ok=0
+  run ip-rules6 ip -6 rule show || rules_ok=0
+  if [ "$rules_ok" = 0 ]; then
+    fail policy_marks "ip rule show failed; no policy rule was checked (evidence ip-rules4.txt ip-rules6.txt)"
+  elif [ -n "$marks" ]; then
+    missing=""
+    nmarks=0
+    for spec in $marks; do
+      IFS=: read -r m pl pu label <<< "$spec"
+      nmarks=$((nmarks + 1))
+      for fam in 4 6; do
+        f="$evdir/ip-rules$fam.txt"
+        grep -qE "^$pl:[[:space:]]+from all fwmark $m lookup (102|meridian_foreign)([[:space:]]|\$)" "$f" || missing="$missing $label/v$fam-lookup"
+        grep -qE "^$pu:[[:space:]]+from all fwmark $m unreachable([[:space:]]|\$)" "$f" || missing="$missing $label/v$fam-unreachable"
+      done
+    done
+    if [ -z "$missing" ]; then
+      pass policy_marks "all $nmarks compiled exit and region-group marks route to table 102 with an unreachable behind them, v4 and v6"
+    else
+      fail policy_marks "loaded policy rules miss:$missing (evidence ip-rules4.txt ip-rules6.txt)"
+    fi
+  fi
+  # Older versions installed "iif <LAN> unreachable" (17850) and "iif mra
+  # unreachable" (17851). With rp_filter on, the kernel's source validation
+  # of a forwarded packet looks the source up with iif = the OUTPUT
+  # interface and mark 0, so those rules dropped every IPv4 packet forwarded
+  # out of the LAN NIC or mra. meridian-routes.sh deletes them.
+  if [ "$rules_ok" = 1 ]; then
+    stale=$(grep -E "^1785[01]:[[:space:]]+from all iif [^[:space:]]+( \[detached\])? unreachable" "$evdir/ip-rules4.txt" )
+    stale=${stale//$'\t'/ }
+    stale=${stale//$'\n'/; }
+    if [ -n "$stale" ]; then
+      fail no_stale_iif_rule "a stale IPv4 'iif … unreachable' rule is loaded ($stale); it breaks source validation of IPv4 forwarded out of that interface (domestic and tunnel replies are dropped); re-run meridian-routes.sh (evidence ip-rules4.txt)"
+    else
+      pass no_stale_iif_rule "no IPv4 'iif … unreachable' rule at 17850/17851"
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  # The kernel's own decision for the paths that must forward.
+  probe_check route_lan_domestic4 "a LAN client ($lan_client4) to a domestic destination ($ros4, mark 0x64)" "$iface" \
+    -4 route get "$ros4" from "$lan_client4" iif "$iface" mark 0x64
+  if [ -n "$tun_ifaces" ]; then
+    probe_tunnels route_tunnel_reply4 "a reply from $foreign4 to the LAN client $lan_client4" "$iface" -4 "$lan_client4" "$foreign4"
+  fi
+  if [ "$has_lan6" = 1 ]; then
+    probe_check route_lan_domestic6 "a LAN client ($lan_client6) to a domestic destination ($domestic6, mark 0x64)" "$iface" \
+      -6 route get "$domestic6" from "$lan_client6" iif "$iface" mark 0x64
+    if [ -n "$tun_ifaces" ]; then
+      probe_tunnels route_tunnel_reply6 "a reply from $foreign6 to the LAN client $lan_client6" "$iface" -6 "$lan_client6" "$foreign6"
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  # Fallback: the foreign table (v4, v6) and the domestic table (v4) end in
+  # a blackhole, so a vanished tunnel or ROS route never falls through.
+  if run route4-102 ip -4 route show table 102 && run route6-102 ip -6 route show table 102 && run route4-100 ip -4 route show table 100; then
+    bh='^blackhole default( .*)? metric 32767([[:space:]]|$)'
+    if grep -qE "$bh" "$evdir/route4-102.txt" && grep -qE "$bh" "$evdir/route6-102.txt" && grep -qE "$bh" "$evdir/route4-100.txt"; then
+      pass fallback_blackholes "tables 102 (v4, v6) and 100 (v4) end in a metric-32767 blackhole"
+    else
+      fail fallback_blackholes "a metric-32767 blackhole default is missing in table 102 or 100 (evidence route4-102.txt route6-102.txt route4-100.txt)"
+    fi
+  else
+    fail fallback_blackholes "ip route show table 102/100 failed (evidence route4-102.txt route6-102.txt route4-100.txt)"
+  fi
+
+  # Remote access: present and wired when enabled, absent when not.
+  if [ "$ra_enabled" = 1 ]; then
+    if run mra-link ip link show dev "$ra_if" && grep -qE '[<,]UP[,>]' "$evdir/mra-link.txt"; then
+      pass remote_iface "$ra_if exists and is up"
+    else
+      fail remote_iface "$ra_if is missing or down (evidence mra-link.txt)"
+    fi
+    probe_check route_remote_domestic4 "a device ($ra_dev4) to a domestic destination ($ros4, mark 0x64)" "$iface" \
+      -4 route get "$ros4" from "$ra_dev4" iif "$ra_if" mark 0x64
+    probe_check route_remote_reply4 "a domestic reply ($ros4, mark 0x64) to a device ($ra_dev4)" "$ra_if" \
+      -4 route get "$ra_dev4" from "$ros4" iif "$iface" mark 0x64
+    probe_check route_remote_reply6 "a domestic reply ($domestic6, mark 0x64) to a device ($ra_dev6)" "$ra_if" \
+      -6 route get "$ra_dev6" from "$domestic6" iif "$iface" mark 0x64
+    if [ "$has_lan6" = 1 ]; then
+      probe_check route_remote_domestic6 "a device ($ra_dev6) to a domestic destination ($domestic6, mark 0x64)" "$iface" \
+        -6 route get "$domestic6" from "$ra_dev6" iif "$ra_if" mark 0x64
+    fi
+    if [ -n "$tun_ifaces" ]; then
+      probe_tunnels route_tunnel_reply_device4 "a reply from $foreign4 to the device $ra_dev4" "$ra_if" -4 "$ra_dev4" "$foreign4"
+      probe_tunnels route_tunnel_reply_device6 "a reply from $foreign6 to the device $ra_dev6" "$ra_if" -6 "$ra_dev6" "$foreign6"
+    fi
+    p4re=${ra_pool4//./\\.}
+    if run ra-route4-main ip -4 route show table main && run ra-route6-main ip -6 route show table main && run ra-route6-100 ip -6 route show table 100 &&
+      grep -qE "^$p4re dev $ra_if( |\$)" "$evdir/ra-route4-main.txt" &&
+      grep -qE "^$p4re dev $ra_if( |\$)" "$evdir/route4-100.txt" &&
+      grep -qF "$ra_pool6 dev $ra_if " "$evdir/ra-route6-main.txt" &&
+      grep -qF "$ra_pool6 dev $ra_if " "$evdir/ra-route6-100.txt"; then
+      pass remote_pool_routes "device pools $ra_pool4 and $ra_pool6 are routed to $ra_if in main and table 100"
+    else
+      fail remote_pool_routes "a device-pool route to $ra_if is missing in main or table 100 (evidence ra-route4-main.txt route4-100.txt ra-route6-main.txt ra-route6-100.txt)"
+    fi
+  else
+    # A stale interface would forward outside the guard's ingress. A
+    # leftover "iif mra unreachable" rule is no_stale_iif_rule's FAIL.
+    if run mra-link ip link show dev "$ra_if"; then
+      fail remote_absent "remote access is off but interface $ra_if exists; the guard does not cover it (evidence mra-link.txt)"
+    else
+      pass remote_absent "remote access is off and there is no $ra_if interface"
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+
+# --- firewall: both tables are required ------------------------------------
+if ! command -v nft >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  fail nft "nft is not installed: there is no Meridian firewall on this host"
+else
+  if run nft-guard nft list table inet meridian_guard; then
+    g="$evdir/nft-guard.txt"
+    if grep -qE 'hook forward priority (-200|filter - 200);' "$g" && grep -q 'fail closed' "$g" && grep -qE "iifname (\"$iface\"|[{] [^}]*\"$iface\"[^}]* [}]) .*drop" "$g"; then
+      pass nft_guard "inet meridian_guard is loaded: forward hook at -200 with the fail-closed LAN drop"
+    else
+      fail nft_guard "inet meridian_guard is loaded but its forward hook or fail-closed drop is missing (evidence nft-guard.txt)"
+    fi
+    # The exit-mark range the guard lets into a tunnel is the compiled one
+    # and holds every compiled mark (nft lists marks as 0x00000101).
+    if [ "$guard_has_exit" = 1 ]; then
+      re='meta mark (0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)-(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+) oifname'
+      gl=$(grep -E 'meta mark 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+-0x[0-9a-fA-F]+ oifname' "$g")
+      if [[ $gl =~ $re ]]; then
+        lo=$((BASH_REMATCH[1])); hi=$((BASH_REMATCH[2])); outside=""
+        for spec in $marks; do
+          m=${spec%%:*}
+          if [ $((m)) -lt "$lo" ] || [ $((m)) -gt "$hi" ]; then outside="$outside $m"; fi
+        done
+        if [ "$lo" -eq $((guard_lo)) ] && [ "$hi" -eq $((guard_hi)) ] && [ -z "$outside" ]; then
+          pass guard_mark_range "guard admits exit marks $guard_lo-$guard_hi into the tunnels, covering every compiled exit and group mark"
+        else
+          fail guard_mark_range "guard range is $(printf '0x%x-0x%x' "$lo" "$hi"), compiled $guard_lo-$guard_hi${outside:+; marks outside:$outside} (evidence nft-guard.txt)"
+        fi
+      else
+        fail guard_mark_range "the guard has no exit-mark range towards the tunnels (evidence nft-guard.txt)"
+      fi
+    fi
+    # Ingress: the LAN NIC, plus mra with the same rules when remote access
+    # is on; never mra when it is off. Only the two LAN-to-device returns
+    # may name the LAN NIC alone.
+    both="iifname [{] (\"$iface\", \"$ra_if\"|\"$ra_if\", \"$iface\") [}]"
+    if [ "$ra_enabled" = 1 ]; then
+      if grep -E "$both .*drop" "$g" | grep -q 'fail closed' &&
+        grep -qE "$both meta l4proto [{] tcp, udp [}] th dport [{] 53, 853 [}] drop" "$g" &&
+        grep -qE "$both meta mark 0x0*64 oifname \"$iface\"" "$g" &&
+        { [ "$guard_has_exit" = 0 ] || grep -qE "$both meta mark 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+-0x[0-9a-fA-F]+ oifname" "$g"; } &&
+        ! grep -E "iifname \"$iface\"" "$g" | grep -qv "oifname \"$ra_if\""; then
+        pass guard_ingress "the guard's ingress is { $iface, $ra_if } with the same DNS drop, mark rules and fail-closed drop"
+      else
+        fail guard_ingress "remote access is on but the guard does not treat $ra_if like $iface (evidence nft-guard.txt)"
+      fi
+    else
+      if grep -q "\"$ra_if\"" "$g"; then
+        fail guard_ingress "remote access is off but the loaded guard names $ra_if (evidence nft-guard.txt)"
+      else
+        pass guard_ingress "the guard's ingress is $iface only"
+      fi
+    fi
+  else
+    fail nft_guard "table inet meridian_guard is not loaded (or not readable; run as root) (evidence nft-guard.txt)"
+  fi
+  if run nft-meridian nft list table inet meridian; then
+    m="$evdir/nft-meridian.txt"
+    if grep -q 'redirect to :53' "$m"; then pass dns_hijack_53 "LAN 53 is redirected to the local resolver"; else fail dns_hijack_53 "no 53 redirect in inet meridian"; fi
+    if grep -q 'redirect to :853' "$m"; then pass dns_hijack_853 "LAN 853 is redirected locally"; else fail dns_hijack_853 "no 853 redirect in inet meridian"; fi
+    if grep -q 'DNS only from the LAN' "$m"; then pass dns_input_drop "non-LAN 53/853 is dropped on input"; else fail dns_input_drop "no non-LAN DNS drop on input"; fi
+    # The ULA drop must be in classify, and nothing ahead of it may classify
+    # an IPv6 destination except the device pool and, when the LAN prefix
+    # is a ULA, exactly that prefix (which must be there).
+    in_cls=0 seen_drop=0 seen_lan=0 ula_bad=""
+    while IFS= read -r l; do
+      case "$l" in *"chain classify {"*) in_cls=1; continue ;; esac
+      [ "$in_cls" = 1 ] || continue
+      case "$l" in *"ip6 daddr fc00::/7 drop"*) seen_drop=1; break ;; esac
+      [[ $l =~ ^[[:space:]]*[}][[:space:]]*$ ]] && break
+      case "$l" in *ip6*|*ipv6*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
+      d=""
+      case "$l" in *"ip6 daddr "*) d=${l#*ip6 daddr }; d=${d%% *} ;; esac
+      case "$l" in *"meta mark set "*" return"*) ;; *) d="" ;; esac
+      if [ -n "$d" ] && [ "$ra_enabled" = 1 ] && [ "$d" = "$ra_pool6" ]; then continue; fi
+      if [ -n "$d" ] && [ -n "$lan6_ula" ] && [ "$d" = "$lan6_ula" ]; then seen_lan=1; continue; fi
+      [ -n "$ula_bad" ] || ula_bad=$l
+    done < "$m"
+    if [ "$seen_drop" != 1 ]; then
+      fail ula_drop "no fc00::/7 drop in the classify chain of inet meridian"
+    elif [ -n "$ula_bad" ]; then
+      fail ula_drop "an IPv6 rule ahead of the fc00::/7 drop lets other addresses past it: ${ula_bad#"${ula_bad%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+    elif [ -n "$lan6_ula" ] && [ "$seen_lan" != 1 ]; then
+      fail ula_drop "the ULA LAN prefix $lan6_ula is not classified ahead of the fc00::/7 drop: home IPv6 hosts are unreachable through the gateway"
+    elif [ -n "$lan6_ula" ]; then
+      pass ula_drop "forwarded ULA is dropped, except the ULA LAN prefix $lan6_ula (home hosts, LAN NIC only)"
+    else
+      pass ula_drop "forwarded ULA is dropped"
+    fi
+    # Domestic split: chnroute (and chnroute6 when clients have IPv6) must
+    # hold elements. They are filled only by a list update and re-added
+    # from the saved batch on every reload; empty means every domestic
+    # address not in another list goes to the default exit.
+    saved="$listsdir/lists/chnroute.nft"
+    for set in chnroute chnroute6; do
+      [ "$set" = chnroute6 ] && [ "$need_chn6" != 1 ] && continue
+      if set_has_elements "$m" "$set"; then
+        pass "${set}_loaded" "nft set $set holds elements"
+      elif [ -s "$saved" ] && grep -q "add element inet meridian $set {" "$saved"; then
+        fail "${set}_loaded" "nft set $set is empty although the saved batch $saved has it: the reload did not re-add it (check meridian-up.sh output for meridian-chnroute-saved-ignored)"
+      else
+        fail "${set}_loaded" "nft set $set is empty: no list update has loaded it on this host (panel 名单 → 更新, or meridian-update-chnroute.sh)"
+      fi
+    done
+    if [ "$ra_enabled" = 1 ]; then
+      if grep -qE "iifname \"$ra_if\" .*redirect to :53" "$m" && grep -qE "iifname \"$ra_if\" .*redirect to :853" "$m" &&
+        grep -E 'dport [{] 53, 853 [}] ip saddr != ' "$m" | grep -qF "$ra_pool4" &&
+        grep -E 'dport [{] 53, 853 [}] ip6 saddr != ' "$m" | grep -qF "$ra_pool6"; then
+        pass remote_dns "53/853 from $ra_if is redirected locally and the DNS input allow-list holds $ra_pool4 and $ra_pool6"
+      else
+        fail remote_dns "the DNS hijack for $ra_if or the device pools in the DNS input allow-list are missing (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+      fi
+      if grep -qE "iifname \"$iface\" udp dport $ra_port accept" "$m" && grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*udp dport $ra_port drop" "$m"; then
+        pass remote_port_lan_only "UDP $ra_port is accepted on $iface only"
+      else
+        fail remote_port_lan_only "the input rules accepting UDP $ra_port on $iface only are missing (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+      fi
+      set -- $marks
+      n4=$(grep -F "ip saddr $ra_pool4 meta mark " "$m" | grep -cE ' snat (ip )?to ')
+      n6=$(grep -F "ip6 saddr $ra_pool6 meta mark " "$m" | grep -cE ' snat (ip6 )?to ')
+      if [ "$n4" -eq $# ] && [ "$n6" -eq $# ] && grep -qF "oifname \"$iface\" ip saddr $ra_pool4 masquerade" "$m" && grep -qF "oifname \"$iface\" ip6 saddr $ra_pool6 masquerade" "$m"; then
+        pass remote_nat "device pools have a transit SNAT for each of the $# marks and a masquerade on $iface"
+      else
+        fail remote_nat "device-pool NAT incomplete: $n4/$# v4 and $n6/$# v6 transit SNAT rules, masquerade on $iface required (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+      fi
+    fi
+    # This host's own exit- and group-marked TCP (the panel's unlock probe,
+    # marked SmartDNS queries) never passes chain mss on forward: chain
+    # local_mss (output) and local_mss_in (input) must clamp it to the same
+    # values as the forward clamp (render_nft.go writeLocalMSS). The values
+    # of each chain are compared as sets; remote-access rules (mra) are a
+    # separate clamp and left out.
+    if [ -n "$tun_ifaces" ]; then
+      # mss_vals CHAIN: the distinct "maxseg size set" values of one chain
+      # of the listing, in order; mss_hook CHAIN: its hook line.
+      mss_vals() {
+        local in=0 l out=" " re='maxseg size set ([0-9]+)'
+        while IFS= read -r l; do
+          if [ "$in" = 0 ]; then case "$l" in *"chain $1 {"*) in=1 ;; esac; continue; fi
+          [[ $l =~ ^[[:space:]]*[}][[:space:]]*$ ]] && break
+          case "$l" in *"\"$ra_if\""*) continue ;; esac
+          [[ $l =~ $re ]] || continue
+          case "$out" in *" ${BASH_REMATCH[1]} "*) ;; *) out="$out${BASH_REMATCH[1]} " ;; esac
+        done < "$m"
+        echo "${out# }"
+      }
+      mss_hook() { grep -A1 -E "chain $1 [{]" "$m" | grep -oE 'hook [a-z]+' | head -n 1; }
+      mss_same() {
+        local v
+        for v in $1; do case " $2" in *" $v "*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; done
+        for v in $2; do case " $1" in *" $v "*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; done
+      }
+      fwd_mss=$(mss_vals mss)
+      loc_mss=$(mss_vals local_mss)
+      locin_mss=$(mss_vals local_mss_in)
+      fwd_ok=1
+      case " $fwd_mss" in *" $mss4 "*) ;; *) fwd_ok=0 ;; esac
+      case " $fwd_mss" in *" $mss6 "*) ;; *) fwd_ok=0 ;; esac
+      if [ -z "$loc_mss" ] || [ "$(mss_hook local_mss)" != "hook output" ]; then
+        fail local_mss "chain local_mss (output) is not loaded: this host's exit-marked TCP (the panel's unlock probe) leaves with the tunnel interface's MSS and stalls where the path MTU is smaller (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+      elif [ -z "$locin_mss" ] || [ "$(mss_hook local_mss_in)" != "hook input" ]; then
+        fail local_mss "chain local_mss_in (input) is not loaded: the SYN-ACK of this host's exit-marked connections is not clamped, so it sends full-size segments into the tunnel (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+      elif [ "$fwd_ok" != 1 ]; then
+        fail local_mss "the forward clamp (chain mss) does not hold the compiled values $mss4/$mss6 (loaded: ${fwd_mss:-none}) (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+      elif ! mss_same "$loc_mss" "$fwd_mss" || ! mss_same "$locin_mss" "$fwd_mss"; then
+        fail local_mss "the local-origin clamp differs from the forward clamp: mss ${fwd_mss}, local_mss ${loc_mss}, local_mss_in ${locin_mss} (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+      else
+        pass local_mss "this host's exit- and group-marked TCP into the tunnels is clamped like forwarded traffic: SYN on output, SYN-ACK on input, values ${fwd_mss}(IPv4 $mss4, IPv6 $mss6)"
+      fi
+    fi
+  else
+    fail nft_meridian "table inet meridian is not loaded (or not readable; run as root) (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+  fi
+fi
+
+# --- another loader that flushes the whole ruleset ------------------------
+# Without both Meridian tables, forwarded LAN traffic is unguarded: IPv4 and
+# IPv6 alike would leave via ROS (there is no routing-level backstop for
+# unmarked traffic). Debian's stock nftables.service loads
+# /etc/nftables.conf, which normally begins by flushing the whole ruleset;
+# whenever it runs after Meridian's tables are loaded (a restart or reload,
+# or a boot order that puts it later) it deletes them while forwarding is on.
+# This is a warning, not a check: whether and when it runs is the host's.
+if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && run nftables-service systemctl is-enabled nftables.service &&
+  [ "$(out_of "$evdir/nftables-service.txt")" = enabled ] &&
+  grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*flush[[:space:]]+ruleset' "$root/etc/nftables.conf" 2>/dev/null; then
+  warn nftables_service_flush "nftables.service is enabled and $root/etc/nftables.conf flushes the whole ruleset: if it runs after Meridian loaded its tables it deletes inet meridian and inet meridian_guard with forwarding on, and LAN IPv4 and IPv6 then leave via ROS unguarded. Disable it (systemctl disable nftables.service) or remove the flush (evidence nftables-service.txt)"
+fi
+
+# --- installed files: the early-boot guard is the main ruleset's guard -----
+if [ ! -f "$nftdir/meridian-guard.nft" ] || [ ! -f "$nftdir/meridian.nft" ]; then
+  fail guard_boot_file "$nftdir/meridian-guard.nft or meridian.nft is missing: meridian-guard.service has nothing to load at boot"
+elif bg=$(guard_block "$nftdir/meridian-guard.nft") && mg=$(guard_block "$nftdir/meridian.nft") && [ "$bg" = "$mg" ]; then
+  printf '%s\n' "$bg" > "$evdir/guard-boot-block.txt"
+  pass guard_boot_file "meridian-guard.nft holds exactly the guard of meridian.nft"
+else
+  printf '%s\n' "${bg:-}" > "$evdir/guard-boot-block.txt"
+  printf '%s\n' "${mg:-}" > "$evdir/guard-main-block.txt"
+  fail guard_boot_file "the early-boot guard differs from the guard in meridian.nft (evidence guard-boot-block.txt guard-main-block.txt)"
+fi
+
+# --- lists: versions are information; an empty domestic domain list fails --
+st="$listsdir/lists/status.json"
+if [ -f "$st" ] && run lists-status cat "$st"; then
+  in=0; name=""; src=""; cnt=""; upd=""; nlist=0
+  while IFS= read -r l; do
+    if [ "$in" = 0 ]; then
+      [ "$l" = '  "published": {' ] && in=1
+      continue
+    fi
+    case "$l" in
+      '  }'*) in=0 ;;
+      '    "'*'": {') name=${l#    \"}; name=${name%\": \{}; src=""; cnt=""; upd="" ;;
+      '      "source": "'*) src=${l#*: \"}; src=${src%\",} ;;
+      '      "updated_at": "'*) upd=${l#*: \"}; upd=${upd%\",} ;;
+      '      "count": '*) cnt=${l#*: }; cnt=${cnt%,} ;;
+      '    }'*) info "list $name" "source=$src count=$cnt updated=$upd"; nlist=$((nlist + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done < "$st"
+  [ "$nlist" -gt 0 ] || info lists "status.json records no published list (evidence lists-status.txt)"
+else
+  info lists "no $st: no list update has run on this host since list sources were added"
+fi
+cn="$listsdir/geosite/cn.txt"
+if [ -f "$cn" ] && grep -qvE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$cn"; then
+  pass geosite_cn "$cn has domains (SmartDNS answers domestic names from domestic resolvers)"
+else
+  fail geosite_cn "$cn is missing or empty: domestic names are resolved abroad; run the list update (panel 名单 → 更新, or meridian-update-geosite.sh)"
+fi
+
+# --- DNS: something listens on 53 for the hijack to land on ----------------
+if ! command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  unknown dns_listener "ss not found; the port 53 listener was not checked"
+elif run ss-udp ss -H -lnu && run ss-tcp ss -H -lnt; then
+  if grep -qE ':53[[:space:]]' "$evdir/ss-udp.txt" && grep -qE ':53[[:space:]]' "$evdir/ss-tcp.txt"; then
+    pass dns_listener "a resolver listens on UDP and TCP 53 (whether it answers correctly is deploy/verify-smartdns.sh)"
+  else
+    fail dns_listener "nothing listens on UDP and TCP 53: the DNS hijack has no resolver behind it (evidence ss-udp.txt ss-tcp.txt)"
+  fi
+else
+  fail dns_listener "ss failed (evidence ss-udp.txt ss-tcp.txt)"
+fi
+
+# --- DNS: no AAAA for tunnelled names (docs/architecture.md「客户端 IPv6 与 AAAA」)
+# With clients_ipv6_via_gateway off the resolver answers AAAA for every name
+# that is not domestic with an empty NOERROR (force-AAAA-SOA): a phone that
+# takes IPv6 from the home router must not get an IPv6 address it would
+# reach over the home line, bypassing the tunnel. One real query for a
+# foreign name (MERIDIAN_VERIFY_AAAA_NAME, default www.google.com; it must
+# not be in a domestic list) to the resolver on 127.0.0.1.
+aaaa_name=${MERIDIAN_VERIFY_AAAA_NAME:-www.google.com}
+if [ "$clients_v6" = 1 ]; then
+  info dns_aaaa_tunnelled "clients_ipv6_via_gateway is on: AAAA is returned for exits and groups with egress_v6 (not checked here); it is only right if every client's IPv6 default route points at this gateway"
+elif [[ ! $aaaa_name =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?(\.[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?)+$ ]]; then
+  fail dns_aaaa_tunnelled "MERIDIAN_VERIFY_AAAA_NAME refused: only a host name"
+else
+  listed="" n=$aaaa_name
+  while [ -n "$n" ]; do
+    # The built-in domestic list as SmartDNS loads it (derived: names a
+    # rule matches are not in it; Apple is not built in any more).
+    f="$listsdir/geosite/ordered/gs_cn.txt"
+    [ -f "$f" ] && grep -qixF -e "$n" -e "-.$n" -e "*.$n" -- "$f" && listed="$n in $f"
+    case "$n" in *.*) n=${n#*.} ;; *) n="" ;; esac
+  done
+  if [ -n "$listed" ]; then
+    unknown dns_aaaa_tunnelled "the test name $aaaa_name is a domestic name ($listed); set MERIDIAN_VERIFY_AAAA_NAME to a foreign name"
+  elif ! command -v dig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    unknown dns_aaaa_tunnelled "dig not found (apt-get install bind9-dnsutils); the AAAA answer for a tunnelled name was not checked"
+  elif run dns-aaaa dig +time=3 +tries=1 @127.0.0.1 AAAA "$aaaa_name"; then
+    if grep -qE '^[^;].*[[:space:]]IN[[:space:]]+AAAA[[:space:]]' "$evdir/dns-aaaa.txt"; then
+      fail dns_aaaa_tunnelled "the resolver returned AAAA for $aaaa_name although clients_ipv6_via_gateway is off: clients would reach it over the home line's IPv6, bypassing the tunnel (evidence dns-aaaa.txt)"
+    elif grep -q 'status: NOERROR' "$evdir/dns-aaaa.txt"; then
+      pass dns_aaaa_tunnelled "AAAA for $aaaa_name is empty (NOERROR, no address): tunnelled names are IPv4-only while clients take IPv6 from the home router (evidence dns-aaaa.txt)"
+    else
+      unknown dns_aaaa_tunnelled "the resolver did not answer AAAA $aaaa_name with NOERROR (evidence dns-aaaa.txt)"
+    fi
+  else
+    unknown dns_aaaa_tunnelled "dig @127.0.0.1 AAAA $aaaa_name got no answer (evidence dns-aaaa.txt)"
+  fi
+fi
+
+# --- DNS: domestic answers for unlisted names (unlisted_domestic_dns) -------
+# SmartDNS sends unlisted names to meridian-dns-split on 127.0.0.1:5356; it
+# accepts a domestic answer only when every address in it is in the China
+# lists it reads at start; empty lists accept nothing (every unlisted name
+# then gets the exit's answer, as with the setting off).
+if [ "$unlisted_dns" = 1 ]; then
+  if ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    unknown dns_split_active "systemctl not found; meridian-dns-split.service was not checked"
+  elif run dns-split-active systemctl is-active meridian-dns-split.service; then
+    pass dns_split_active "meridian-dns-split.service is active (evidence dns-split-active.txt)"
+  else
+    fail dns_split_active "meridian-dns-split.service is not active: SmartDNS's only upstream for unlisted names is down, they get SERVFAIL (evidence dns-split-active.txt; journalctl -u meridian-dns-split)"
+  fi
+  bad=""
+  for f in "$listsdir/lists/china.txt" "$listsdir/lists/china6.txt"; do
+    if [ ! -f "$f" ] || ! grep -qvE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$f"; then
+      bad="$bad $f"
+    fi
+  done
+  if [ -z "$bad" ]; then
+    pass unlisted_domestic_lists "the China lists meridian-dns-split checks domestic answers against are present (an unlisted name gets the domestic answer only when every address in it is a China address)"
+  else
+    fail unlisted_domestic_lists "missing or empty:$bad — no domestic answer is accepted for unlisted names; run the list update (panel 名单 → 更新, or meridian-update-chnroute.sh)"
+  fi
+  info unlisted_domestic_dns "on: the domestic resolvers see every unlisted name, foreign ones included; those queries leave this gateway directly over the home line"
+fi
+
+# --- region-group DNS (docs/architecture.md「地区组的解析」) -----------------
+# Each group the hub switches is resolved at its own resolver address with
+# its own mark. What this host can show: the SNAT of its own marked queries
+# is loaded, SmartDNS's config asks each group's resolver with the mark in
+# decimal, and a marked lookup of each resolver address goes into a tunnel
+# (never the LAN port). Whether a member answers, and whether the answer
+# follows a failover, is only visible end to end (PENDING-HUMAN below).
+if [ -n "$grp_dns" ]; then
+  nm="$evdir/nft-meridian.txt"
+  if [ -f "$nm" ] && grep -qx 'exit=0' "$nm"; then
+    missing=""
+    while read -r lbl res mhex mdec transit dg; do
+      [ -n "$lbl" ] || continue
+      grep -F "ip6 daddr $res " "$nm" | grep -F "snat ip6 to $transit" | grep -qE "meta mark 0x0*${mhex#0x}( |\$)" || missing="$missing $lbl"
+    done <<< "$grp_dns"
+    if [ -z "$missing" ]; then
+      pass group_dns_snat "this host's marked queries to each group resolver are SNATed to the group's transit address"
+    else
+      fail group_dns_snat "no resolver SNAT loaded for group(s):$missing (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+    fi
+  else
+    fail group_dns_snat "table inet meridian could not be listed; the group resolver SNAT was not checked (evidence nft-meridian.txt)"
+  fi
+  conf="$root/etc/smartdns/smartdns.conf"
+  if [ ! -r "$conf" ]; then
+    unknown group_dns_upstream "$conf is not readable; the group resolver upstreams were not checked"
+  else
+    missing=""
+    while read -r lbl res mhex mdec transit dg; do
+      [ -n "$lbl" ] || continue
+      grep -E "^server $res -group $dg( |\$)" "$conf" | grep -qE " -set-mark $mdec( |\$)" || missing="$missing $lbl"
+    done <<< "$grp_dns"
+    if grep -qE '^server .*-set-mark 0[xX]' "$conf"; then
+      fail group_dns_upstream "$conf writes a -set-mark in hex: SmartDNS accepts it and applies no mark"
+    elif [ -z "$missing" ]; then
+      pass group_dns_upstream "$conf asks each group's resolver address with the group mark (decimal)"
+    else
+      fail group_dns_upstream "$conf has no marked resolver upstream for group(s):$missing"
+    fi
+  fi
+  if ! command -v ip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    unknown group_dns_route "ip not found; the marked route to the group resolvers was not checked"
+  else
+    bad=""
+    while read -r lbl res mhex mdec transit dg; do
+      [ -n "$lbl" ] || continue
+      n="rtget-group-dns-$lbl"
+      run "$n" ip -6 route get "$res" mark "$mhex"
+      IFS= read -r first < "$evdir/$n.txt"
+      dev=""
+      [[ $first =~ \ dev\ ([^ ]+) ]] && dev=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
+      ok=0
+      if [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ -n "$dev" ]; then
+        case "$first" in
+          unreachable*|blackhole*|prohibit*) ;;
+          *) case " $tun_ifaces " in *" $dev "*) ok=1 ;; esac ;;
+        esac
+      fi
+      [ "$ok" = 1 ] || bad="$bad $lbl: $first (evidence $n.txt);"
+    done <<< "$grp_dns"
+    if [ -z "$bad" ]; then
+      pass group_dns_route "a lookup of each group resolver address with the group mark resolves into a tunnel ($tun_ifaces), not $iface"
+    else
+      fail group_dns_route "a marked lookup of a group resolver address does not enter a tunnel:$bad"
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+
+# --- remote access: WireGuard state of mra (public keys only) --------------
+if [ "$ra_enabled" = 1 ]; then
+  if ! command -v wg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    fail remote_wg "wg (wireguard-tools) is not installed: $ra_if cannot be configured"
+  else
+    if run mra-port wg show "$ra_if" listen-port && [ "$(out_of "$evdir/mra-port.txt")" = "$ra_port" ]; then
+      pass remote_listen "$ra_if listens on UDP $ra_port"
+    else
+      fail remote_listen "$ra_if does not listen on UDP $ra_port (evidence mra-port.txt)"
+    fi
+    if run mra-peers wg show "$ra_if" peers; then
+      missing=""; extra=0; npeer=0
+      while read -r k id; do
+        [ -n "$k" ] || continue
+        npeer=$((npeer + 1))
+        grep -qxF -- "$k" "$evdir/mra-peers.txt" || missing="$missing $id"
+      done <<< "$ra_peers"
+      while IFS= read -r k; do
+        case "$k" in ''|exit=*) continue ;; esac
+        case "$ra_peers" in "$k "*|*"
+$k "*) ;; *) extra=$((extra + 1)) ;; esac
+      done < "$evdir/mra-peers.txt"
+      if [ -z "$missing" ] && [ "$extra" = 0 ]; then
+        pass remote_peers "$ra_if has exactly the $npeer enabled devices as peers (public keys compared)"
+      else
+        fail remote_peers "$ra_if peers differ from the enabled devices:${missing:+ missing$missing;} $extra unexpected (evidence mra-peers.txt)"
+      fi
+    else
+      fail remote_peers "wg show $ra_if peers failed (evidence mra-peers.txt)"
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+
+# --- ROS fd00::/8 blackhole: only from a real read-only query --------------
+ros_ssh=${MERIDIAN_ROS_SSH:-}
+if [ -z "$ros_ssh" ]; then
+  pending ros_ula_blackhole "not executed. On ROS (read-only): /ipv6 route print where blackhole and (dst-address=fd00::/8 or dst-address=fc00::/7); archive the output, or rerun with MERIDIAN_ROS_SSH=user@$ros4"
+else
+  case "$ros_ssh" in
+    -*|*[!A-Za-z0-9@._:-]*)
+      fail ros_ula_blackhole "MERIDIAN_ROS_SSH refused: only user@host"
+      ;;
+    *)
+      if command -v ssh >/dev/null 2>&1 && run ros-ipv6-blackhole ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 -- "$ros_ssh" '/ipv6 route print terse where blackhole'; then
+        if grep -qE 'dst-address=(fd00::/8|fc00::/7)' "$evdir/ros-ipv6-blackhole.txt"; then
+          pass ros_ula_blackhole "ROS has a ULA blackhole (evidence ros-ipv6-blackhole.txt)"
+        else
+          fail ros_ula_blackhole "ROS answered but has no fd00::/8 or fc00::/7 blackhole (evidence ros-ipv6-blackhole.txt)"
+        fi
+      else
+        unknown ros_ula_blackhole "could not query ROS over ssh; nothing was checked (evidence ros-ipv6-blackhole.txt)"
+      fi
+      ;;
+  esac
+fi
+
+# --- tunnel interface MTU ---------------------------------------------------
+# Every WireGuard interface of this gateway must run with the MTU its config
+# sets ("MTU =" in /etc/wireguard/IF.conf; meridian-up.sh sets an existing
+# interface in place after wg syncconf, which itself keeps the old MTU). A
+# difference means an adopted MTU is not in effect: FAIL, never PASS.
+if [ -n "$tun_mtus" ]; then
+  if ! command -v ip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    unknown tunnel_mtu "ip not found; the running tunnel MTUs were not checked"
+  else
+    mtu_bad=""; mtu_ok=""
+    for spec in $tun_mtus; do
+      mtu_if=${spec%%:*}; mtu_want=${spec##*:}
+      if run "link-$mtu_if" ip link show dev "$mtu_if"; then
+        mtu_have=$(out_of "$evdir/link-$mtu_if.txt" | grep -oE ' mtu [0-9]+' | head -n 1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
+        if [ "$mtu_have" = "$mtu_want" ]; then
+          mtu_ok="$mtu_ok $mtu_if=$mtu_want"
+        else
+          mtu_bad="$mtu_bad $mtu_if(running ${mtu_have:-?}, config $mtu_want)"
+        fi
+      else
+        mtu_bad="$mtu_bad $mtu_if(not present, config $mtu_want)"
+      fi
+    done
+    if [ -n "$mtu_bad" ]; then
+      fail tunnel_mtu "running MTU differs from the config for:$mtu_bad; an adopted MTU is not in effect until meridian-up.sh runs again (it sets the MTU in place) (evidence link-*.txt)"
+    else
+      pass tunnel_mtu "every tunnel interface runs with its config's MTU:$mtu_ok"
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+
+# --- not executable from this script ---------------------------------------
+if [ "$unlisted_dns" = 1 ]; then
+  pending dns_leak_client "dnsleaktest.com and ipleak.net on the test device (v4 and v6), plus a WAN capture with no 53/853 from the device itself; this script runs no browser. unlisted_domestic_dns is on: the leak sites list the domestic resolvers next to the exit's (their test names are unlisted, so this gateway asks the domestic resolvers too), and this gateway sends unlisted names, foreign ones included, to them over the home line; that is the expected result with the setting on, not a leak of the device"
+else
+  pending dns_leak_client "dnsleaktest.com and ipleak.net on the test device (v4 and v6), plus a WAN capture with no 53/853 from it; this script runs no browser"
