+#!/bin/bash
+# Return path follows whichever west tunnel is actually up: IX, relay WSS, then gateway WSS.
+set -u
+IX_MODE=0
+IX=""
+ALI_WSS=""
+HOME_WSS="m04"
+IX_PEER=""
+ALI_PEER=""
+HOME_PEER="10.66.5.1"
+LAN="192.168.77.0/24"
+TRANSIT4="10.66.200.0/24"
+TRANSIT6="fd66:0:0:ff::/64"
+LAN6="2001:db8:77::/64"
+FAILS_NEED=3
+RECOVERS_NEED=5
+COOLDOWN=120
+GROUP_PLAN=3066dbf6b0653d936660be38
+MESH_DEV=mmesh
+MESH_NH4=169.254.66.2
+MESH_NH6=fe80::66:2
+GROUP_TABLES="210 211 212 213 214 215 216"
+
+group_hop() {
+  local table="$1" dev="$2"
+  case "$table" in
+    ""|main|100|102|150)
+      echo "group hop refused on table $table" >&2
+      return 1
+      ;;
+  esac
+  case " $GROUP_TABLES " in
+    *" $table "*) ;;
+    *)
+      echo "group hop refused on table $table: not a region-group table" >&2
+      return 1
+      ;;
+  esac
+  [ -n "$dev" ] || return 1
+  local nh4="" nh6=""
+  case "$dev" in
+    *"|"*) nh4="${dev#*|}"; nh6="${nh4#*|}"; nh4="${nh4%%|*}"; dev="${dev%%|*}" ;;
+  esac
+  if [ "${dev%%|*}" = "$MESH_DEV" ]; then
+    # The Mesh veth carries only WireGuard's outer packets to the exits' Mesh
+    # addresses (mesh_underlay). It is never the next hop of a table.
+    echo "group hop refused on table $table: $MESH_DEV is never a next hop" >&2
+    return 1
+  elif [ -n "$nh4" ] && [ -n "$nh6" ]; then
+    # A member behind another exit's tunnel (nested or external exit): the
+    # same device, told apart by next hop; the hub's nested_snat chain gives
+    # the group's packets that member's own transit source.
+    ip route replace default via "$nh4" dev "$dev" onlink table "$table"
+    ip -6 route replace default via "$nh6" dev "$dev" onlink table "$table"
+  else
+    ip route replace default dev "$dev" table "$table"
+    ip -6 route replace default dev "$dev" table "$table"
+  fi
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$table"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$table"
+}
+
+group_can_return() {
+  local dir="$1" target="$2" now="$3" last="$4" st lo ok
+  st=$(cat "$dir/$target.state" 2>/dev/null || echo up)
+  lo=$(cat "$dir/$target.lastok" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+  ok=$(cat "$dir/$target.okst" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  case "$ok" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
+  [ "$st" = "up" ] && [ "$lo" = "1" ] || return 1
+  [ $((now-ok)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" ] || return 1
+  [ "$last" -eq 0 ] || [ $((now-last)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" ]
+}
+group_step() {
+  local gid="$1" table="$2" target="$3" mesh="$4" hold="$5" manual="$6" treason="$7"
+  shift 7
+  local dir="/run/meridian/group/${gid}"
+  mkdir -p "$dir" /run/meridian/group-iface
+  local now id iface peer fails goods state okst lastok ids="" t_up=0 alt_id="" pairs=""
+  now=$(date +%s)
+  while [ $# -ge 3 ]; do
+    id="$1"; iface="$2"; peer="$3"; shift 3
+    ids="$ids $id"
+    pairs="$pairs $id=$iface"
+    echo "$iface" > "/run/meridian/group-iface/${id}"
+    fails=$(cat "$dir/$id.fails" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    goods=$(cat "$dir/$id.goods" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    state=$(cat "$dir/$id.state" 2>/dev/null || echo up)
+    okst=$(cat "$dir/$id.okst" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    case "$fails" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fails=0 ;; esac
+    case "$goods" in ''|*[!0-9]*) goods=0 ;; esac
+    [ "$state" = "down" ] || state=up
+    if alive "${iface%%|*}" "$peer"; then
+      lastok=1
+      [ -n "$okst" ] || okst="$now"
+      fails=0
+      if [ "$state" = "down" ]; then
+        goods=$((goods+1))
+        if [ "$goods" -ge "$RECOVERS_NEED" ]; then state=up; goods=0; fi
+      else
+        goods=0
+      fi
+    else

+group_table_default() {
+  local fam="$1" table="$2" out line floor=0 i via

+          return 0
+        fi
+      done
+      echo other; return 0

+group_table_hop() {

+    echo "reason $reason"
+    echo "alert $alert"
+    echo "switched $switched"

+    if alive "$IX" "$IX_PEER"; then echo "$IX"; return; fi
+    echo "$HOME_WSS"; return
+  fi
+  if alive "$IX" "$IX_PEER"; then echo "$IX"; return; fi

+    echo "meridian-rule-heal: policy rule $RULE_SENTINEL was missing; re-ran meridian-routes.sh, restarting the failover loop" >&2
+    exec "$0"
+  fi
+  if [ "$rule_missing" -eq 2 ]; then echo "meridian-rule-heal: policy rule $RULE_SENTINEL is missing and meridian-routes.sh failed; retrying every 5 s" >&2; fi

+  rule_heal

+      cur="$want"
+      bad=0
+    fi
+  else
+    bad=0
+  fi
+  check_groups || true
+  sleep 5
+done

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-9895c356
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m04 -o m05"
+  "-i m05 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m06"
+  "-i m06 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m07"
+  "-i m07 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m08"
+  "-i m08 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m09"
+  "-i m09 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m10"
+  "-i m10 -o m04"
+  "-i m04 -o m11"
+  "-i m11 -o m04"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+# managed tunnels, the interface the topology names, mra/mmesh). The kernel
+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the
+# interface value is what matters here. Other interfaces are not touched.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=any
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_RA_STATE=/var/lib/meridian/node/ra-accept
+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" ]; then ra_old=$(cat "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"); fi
+for ra_if in $(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ra_now" "$ra_old" | sort -u); do
+  case "$ra_if" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) continue ;; esac
+  ra_f=/proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra
+  [ -r "$ra_f" ] || continue
+  ra_cur=$(head -c 8 "$ra_f")
+  case "$ra_cur" in
+    2) ;;
+    1)
+      if ! sysctl -w "net/ipv6/conf/$ra_if/accept_ra=2" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-ra-failed: could not set accept_ra=2 on $ra_if; IPv6 forwarding not enabled" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi
+      echo "meridian-ra: $ra_if accept_ra 1 -> 2 (keeps its router advertisements with IPv6 forwarding on)" ;;
+    *)
+      case " $(printf '%s ' $ra_now) " in
+        *" $ra_if "*)
+          echo "meridian-ra-unmanaged: $ra_if has RA-learned IPv6 routes but accept_ra=$ra_cur (a userspace RA client); IPv6 forwarding could break it, so forwarding is not enabled" >&2
+          exit 1 ;;
+      esac
+      continue ;;
+  esac
+  install -d -m 700 "${MERIDIAN_RA_STATE%/*}"
+  grep -qx -- "$ra_if" "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$ra_if" >> "$MERIDIAN_RA_STATE"
+done
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+# The MTU each tunnel interface's config sets ("MTU ="): wg syncconf keeps the
+# running interface MTU, so an existing interface is aligned in place below.
+wg_conf_mtu() {
+  case "$1" in
+    m04) echo 1360 ;;
+    m05) echo 1420 ;;
+    m06) echo 1420 ;;
+    m07) echo 1420 ;;
+    m08) echo 1420 ;;
+    m09) echo 1420 ;;
+    m10) echo 1420 ;;
+    m11) echo 1420 ;;
+    *) echo "" ;;
+  esac
+}
+for iface in m04 m05 m06 m07 m08 m09 m10 m11; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+    want_mtu=$(wg_conf_mtu "$iface")
+    have_mtu=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$iface/mtu" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [ -n "$want_mtu" ] && [ "$have_mtu" != "$want_mtu" ]; then
+      ip link set dev "$iface" mtu "$want_mtu"
+      echo "meridian-wg-mtu: $iface ${have_mtu:-?} -> $want_mtu (set in place; the tunnel stays up)"
+    fi
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+if [ -e /lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ] || [ -e /usr/lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ]; then
+  nd=/etc/systemd/networkd.conf.d/90-meridian.conf
+  nd_want='# meridian: keep Meridian ip rules and routes when systemd-networkd restarts
+[Network]
+ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=no
+ManageForeignRoutes=no'
+  if [ "$(cat "$nd" 2>/dev/null)" != "$nd_want" ]; then
+    if mkdir -p "${nd%/*}" && printf '%s\n' "$nd_want" > "$nd.tmp" && chmod 0644 "$nd.tmp" && mv -f "$nd.tmp" "$nd"; then
+      echo "meridian-networkd: wrote $nd (networkd not restarted; it applies at its next start)"
+    else
+      rm -f "$nd.tmp"
+      echo "meridian-networkd: could not write $nd; a networkd restart would delete the Meridian ip rules" >&2
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit 'wstunnel-meridian.service'
+enable_unit meridian-failover.service
+systemctl restart meridian-failover.service
+echo meridian-up-complete

+#!/bin/bash
+# Return path follows whichever west tunnel is actually up: IX, relay WSS, then gateway WSS.
+set -u
+IX_MODE=0
+IX="m01"
+ALI_WSS=""
+HOME_WSS=""
+IX_PEER="10.66.2.1"
+ALI_PEER=""
+HOME_PEER=""
+LAN="192.168.77.0/24"
+TRANSIT4="10.66.200.0/24"
+TRANSIT6="fd66:0:0:ff::/64"
+LAN6="2001:db8:77::/64"
+FAILS_NEED=3
+RECOVERS_NEED=5
+COOLDOWN=120
+GROUP_PLAN=a550b2f7c7edf95e5e16ff4f
+MQ_PLAN=1a21a5db65611ea3dc1806a7
+MQ_WINDOW=6
+MQ_LOSS=150
+MQ_RTT=400
+MQ_RETURN=120
+MQ_DWELL=120
+MQ_ADV=25
+
+mesh_sample() {
+ local iface="$1" peer="$2" file="$3" out
+ if [ -z "$iface" ]; then echo '5 0 0' > "$file"; return; fi
+ out=$(LC_ALL=C ping -n -q -I "$iface" -c 5 -i 0.2 -W 1 -w 3 "$peer" 2>/dev/null || true)
+ awk '/packets transmitted/ {s=$1;r=$4} /min\/avg\/max/ {split($4,a,"/"); ms=int(a[2])} END {if(s<1)s=5; print s,r+0,ms+0}' <<< "$out" > "$file"
+}
+mesh_route() {
+ local table="$1" dev="$2" fam failed=0
+ for fam in -4 -6; do
+  ip "$fam" route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$table" || failed=1
+  if [ "$dev" = blackhole ]; then
+   ip "$fam" route replace blackhole default table "$table" || failed=1
+  else
+   ip "$fam" route replace default dev "$dev" table "$table" || failed=1
+  fi
+ done
+ if [ "$failed" = 1 ]; then
+  # A partial dual-stack update must fail closed on both families.
+  ip -4 route replace blackhole default table "$table" || true
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default table "$table" || true
+  return 1
+ fi
+}
+mesh_leg_step() {
+ local id="$1" table="$2" direct="$3" dp="$4" mesh="$5" mp="$6" resolver="$7" ds="${8:-}" ms="${9:-}" src
+ local dir="/run/meridian/exit-legs/$id" now old=direct switched=0 good=0 active reason dl dr ml mr dev result=ok tmp
+ mkdir -p "$dir"
+ now=$(date +%s)
+ if [ "$(cat "$dir/plan" 2>/dev/null)" != "$MQ_PLAN" ]; then
+  rm -f "$dir/window" "$dir/state" "$dir/events"
+  echo "$MQ_PLAN" > "$dir/plan"
+ fi
+ if [ -f "$dir/state" ]; then read -r old switched good < "$dir/state"; fi
+ case "$old" in direct|mesh|blackhole) ;; *) old=blackhole; switched=0; good=0 ;; esac
+ mesh_sample "$direct" "$dp" "$dir/d" & local pid=$!
+ mesh_sample "$mesh" "$mp" "$dir/m"
+ wait "$pid"
+ paste -d ' ' "$dir/d" "$dir/m" >> "$dir/window"
+ tail -n "$MQ_WINDOW" "$dir/window" > "$dir/window.tmp" && mv -f "$dir/window.tmp" "$dir/window"
+ read -r active switched good reason dl dr ml mr < <(awk -v now="$now" -v old="$old" -v sw="$switched" -v good="$good" -v win="$MQ_WINDOW" -v loss="$MQ_LOSS" -v rtt="$MQ_RTT" -v ret="$MQ_RETURN" -v dwell="$MQ_DWELL" -v adv="$MQ_ADV" '
+ {ds+=$1;dc+=$2;dt+=$2*$3;ms+=$4;mc+=$5;mt+=$5*$6;du=($2>0);mu=($5>0);lastgood=du && ($1-$2)*1000/$1<loss && $3<rtt}
+ END {
+ dl=ds?int((ds-dc)*1000/ds):1000;dr=dc?int(dt/dc):0;ml=ms?int((ms-mc)*1000/ms):1000;mr=mc?int(mt/mc):0
+ ok=du && dl<loss && dr<rtt && lastgood
+ if(ok){if(!good)good=now}else good=0
+ want=old;why="stable";ready=(!sw || now-sw>=dwell)
+ if(!du && !mu){want="blackhole";why="both_down"}
+ else if(old=="direct" && !du){want="mesh";why="direct_down"}
+ else if(old=="mesh" && !mu && du){want="direct";why="mesh_down"}
+ else if(old=="blackhole"){want=du?"direct":"mesh";why="reachable"}
+ else if(old=="direct" && mu && NR>=win && ready && (mr+ml)*(100+adv)<(dr+dl)*100){want="mesh";why="quality"}
+ else if(old=="mesh" && ok && NR>=win && good && now-good>=ret && ready && (dr+dl)*100<=(mr+ml)*(100+adv)){want="direct";why="direct_recovered"}
+ if(want!=old)sw=now
+ print want,sw,good,why,dl,dr,ml,mr
+ }' "$dir/window")
+ case "$active" in direct) dev="$direct" ;; mesh) dev="$mesh" ;; *) active=blackhole; dev=blackhole ;; esac
+ [ -n "$dev" ] || { active=blackhole; dev=blackhole; }
+ if ! mesh_route "$table" "$dev"; then active=blackhole; dev=blackhole; result=failed; reason=route_failed; fi
+ if [ -n "$resolver" ]; then
+  src="$ds"; [ "$dev" != "$mesh" ] || src="$ms"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole "$resolver/128" metric 32767 || result=failed
+  if [ "$dev" = blackhole ]; then
+   ip -6 route replace blackhole "$resolver/128" || result=failed
+  else
+   ip -6 route replace "$resolver/128" dev "$dev" ${src:+src "$src"} || result=failed
+  fi
+  if [ "$result" = failed ]; then
+   active=blackhole; dev=blackhole; reason=route_failed
+   mesh_route "$table" blackhole || true
+   ip -6 route replace blackhole "$resolver/128" || true
+  fi
+ fi
+ # Only publish a device that was applied successfully. Groups fail closed.
+ echo "$dev" > "$dir/iface.tmp" && mv -f "$dir/iface.tmp" "$dir/iface"
+ echo "$active $switched $good" > "$dir/state.tmp" && mv -f "$dir/state.tmp" "$dir/state"
+ tmp="$dir/report.tmp"
+ echo "leg $MQ_PLAN $id $now $active $reason $switched $dl $dr $ml $mr $result" > "$tmp" && mv -f "$tmp" "$dir/report"
+ if [ "$old" != "$active" ] || [ "$result" != ok ]; then
+  echo "leg-event $MQ_PLAN $id $now $active $reason $switched $dl $dr $ml $mr $result" >> "$dir/events"
+  tail -n 32 "$dir/events" > "$dir/events.tmp" && mv -f "$dir/events.tmp" "$dir/events"
+  echo "exit-leg $id $old -> $active reason=$reason direct_loss=$dl direct_rtt_ms=$dr mesh_loss=$ml mesh_rtt_ms=$mr result=$result" >&2
+ fi
+}
+mesh_managed() {
+ case "$1" in
+ 'jp-a') return 0 ;;
+ *) return 1 ;;
+ esac
+}
+mesh_member_alive() {
+ local id="$1" iface="$2" peer="$3" gid="$4" target="$5" active
+ if mesh_managed "$id"; then
+  [ "$(mesh_selected "$iface")" != blackhole ] && return 0
+  active=$(cat "/run/meridian/group/$gid/active" 2>/dev/null || echo "$target")
+  [ "$active" = "$id" ]; return
+ fi
+ alive "$iface" "$peer"
+}
+mesh_selected() {
+ case "$1" in
+ 'm15'|'m20') cat /run/meridian/exit-legs/jp-a/iface 2>/dev/null || echo blackhole ;;
+ *) echo "$1" ;;
+ esac
+}
+check_mesh_legs() {
+ local -a mq_jobs=()
+ local mq_pid
+ mkdir -p /run/meridian/exit-legs
+ mesh_leg_step 'jp-a' 204 'm15' '10.66.16.2' 'm20' '10.66.21.2' 'fd66::54:4' '' '' &
+ mq_jobs+=("$!")
+ if [ ${#mq_jobs[@]} -ge 8 ]; then for mq_pid in "${mq_jobs[@]}"; do wait "$mq_pid" || true; done; mq_jobs=(); fi
+ for mq_pid in "${mq_jobs[@]}"; do wait "$mq_pid" || true; done
+ {
+ cat '/run/meridian/exit-legs/jp-a/report' '/run/meridian/exit-legs/jp-a/events'
+ } 2>/dev/null > /run/meridian/exit-legs/report.tmp
+ mv -f /run/meridian/exit-legs/report.tmp /run/meridian/exit-legs/report
+}
+mesh_underlay() {
+  local a keep='10.68.0.1' live=''
+  for a in $keep; do
+    ip route replace blackhole "$a/32" metric 32767 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    case " $live " in
+      *" $a "*) up=1 ;;
+      *) up=0 ;;
+    esac
+    if [ "$up" = 1 ] && [ -n "$(ip link show 'CloudflareWARP' up 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
+      ip route replace "$a/32" dev 'CloudflareWARP' || echo "Mesh underlay route to $a not installed; that Mesh leg stays down" >&2
+    else
+      ip route del "$a/32" dev 'CloudflareWARP' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    fi
+  done
+  return 0
+}
+MESH_DEV=mmesh
+MESH_NH4=169.254.66.2
+MESH_NH6=fe80::66:2
+GROUP_TABLES="210 211 212 213 214 215 216"
+
+group_hop() {
+  local table="$1" dev="$2"
+  case "$table" in
+    ""|main|100|102|150)
+      echo "group hop refused on table $table" >&2
+      return 1
+      ;;
+  esac
+  case " $GROUP_TABLES " in
+    *" $table "*) ;;
+    *)
+      echo "group hop refused on table $table: not a region-group table" >&2
+      return 1
+      ;;
+  esac
+  dev=$(mesh_selected "$dev")
+  [ -n "$dev" ] || return 1
+  if [ "$dev" = blackhole ]; then mesh_route "$table" blackhole; return; fi
+  local nh4="" nh6=""
+  case "$dev" in
+    *"|"*) nh4="${dev#*|}"; nh6="${nh4#*|}"; nh4="${nh4%%|*}"; dev="${dev%%|*}" ;;
+  esac
+  if [ "${dev%%|*}" = "$MESH_DEV" ]; then
+    # The Mesh veth carries only WireGuard's outer packets to the exits' Mesh
+    # addresses (mesh_underlay). It is never the next hop of a table.
+    echo "group hop refused on table $table: $MESH_DEV is never a next hop" >&2
+    return 1
+  elif [ -n "$nh4" ] && [ -n "$nh6" ]; then
+    # A member behind another exit's tunnel (nested or external exit): the
+    # same device, told apart by next hop; the hub's nested_snat chain gives
+    # the group's packets that member's own transit source.
+    ip route replace default via "$nh4" dev "$dev" onlink table "$table"
+    ip -6 route replace default via "$nh6" dev "$dev" onlink table "$table"
+  else
+    ip route replace default dev "$dev" table "$table"
+    ip -6 route replace default dev "$dev" table "$table"
+  fi
+  ip route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$table"
+  ip -6 route replace blackhole default metric 32767 table "$table"
+}
+
+group_can_return() {
+  local dir="$1" target="$2" now="$3" last="$4" st lo ok
+  st=$(cat "$dir/$target.state" 2>/dev/null || echo up)
+  lo=$(cat "$dir/$target.lastok" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+  ok=$(cat "$dir/$target.okst" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  case "$ok" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
+  [ "$st" = "up" ] && [ "$lo" = "1" ] || return 1
+  [ $((now-ok)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" ] || return 1
+  [ "$last" -eq 0 ] || [ $((now-last)) -ge "$COOLDOWN" ]
+}
+group_step() {
+  local gid="$1" table="$2" target="$3" mesh="$4" hold="$5" manual="$6" treason="$7"
+  shift 7
+  local dir="/run/meridian/group/${gid}"
+  mkdir -p "$dir" /run/meridian/group-iface
+  local now id iface peer fails goods state okst lastok ids="" t_up=0 alt_id="" pairs=""
+  now=$(date +%s)
+  while [ $# -ge 3 ]; do
+    id="$1"; iface="$2"; peer="$3"; shift 3
+    ids="$ids $id"
+    pairs="$pairs $id=$(mesh_selected "$iface")"
+    echo "$iface" > "/run/meridian/group-iface/${id}"
+    fails=$(cat "$dir/$id.fails" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    goods=$(cat "$dir/$id.goods" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    state=$(cat "$dir/$id.state" 2>/dev/null || echo up)
+    okst=$(cat "$dir/$id.okst" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    case "$fails" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fails=0 ;; esac
+    case "$goods" in ''|*[!0-9]*) goods=0 ;; esac
+    [ "$state" = "down" ] || state=up
+    if alive "${iface%%|*}" "$peer"; then
+      lastok=1
+      [ -n "$okst" ] || okst="$now"
+      fails=0
+      if [ "$state" = "down" ]; then
+        goods=$((goods+1))
+        if [ "$goods" -ge "$RECOVERS_NEED" ]; then state=up; goods=0; fi
+      else
+        goods=0
+      fi
+    else

+group_table_default() {
+  local fam="$1" table="$2" out line floor=0 i via
+  local -a w

+    read -r -a w <<< "$line"
+    [ "${#w[@]}" -gt 0 ] || continue
+    case " $line " in
+      *" metric 32767 "*)

+        ;;
+    esac
+    if [ "${w[0]}" = default ]; then
+      via=""
+      for ((i=1; i<${#w[@]}-1; i++)); do

+      done

+          if [ -n "$via" ]; then echo "dev:${w[$((i+1))]}@$via"; else echo "dev:${w[$((i+1))]}"; fi
+          return 0

+      echo other; return 0

+    if [ "${w[1]:-}" = default ]; then

+group_record() {

+    echo "group $gid"
+    echo "plan $GROUP_PLAN"
+    echo "beat $now"
+    echo "hop $hop"
+    echo "active $active"
+    echo "reason $reason"
+    echo "alert $alert"
+    echo "switched $switched"
+    echo "result $result"

+    if [ -n "$lastfail" ]; then echo "lastfail $lastfail"; fi

+    fi

+    bad=0
+  fi

+  check_groups || true

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-dcd39b54
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m00 -o m12"
+  "-i m12 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m13"
+  "-i m13 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m14"
+  "-i m14 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m15"
+  "-i m15 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m16"
+  "-i m16 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m17"
+  "-i m17 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m18"
+  "-i m18 -o m00"
+  "-i m00 -o m20"
+  "-i m20 -o m00"
+  "-i m01 -o m12"
+  "-i m12 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m13"
+  "-i m13 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m14"
+  "-i m14 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m15"
+  "-i m15 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m16"
+  "-i m16 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m17"
+  "-i m17 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m18"
+  "-i m18 -o m01"
+  "-i m01 -o m20"
+  "-i m20 -o m01"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash

+# rp_filter=2 and no ICMP redirects on Meridian's interfaces only (the
+# managed tunnels, the interface the topology names, mra/mmesh). The kernel
+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the
+# interface value is what matters here. Other interfaces are not touched.
+harden_sysctl() {
+  local i

+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv6.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  done

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=any
+# meridian-ix-hub: ingress=198.51.100.10 iface=- egress=203.0.113.20
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi

+ra_now=$(ip -6 route show table main proto ra 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<NF;i++) if ($i=="dev") print $(i+1)}' | sort -u) || ra_now=""
+ra_old=""

===== nodes/jp-a/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-55c24cc8
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m08 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m08 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m15 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m15 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m20 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m20 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Policy routes for one Meridian node. Safe to re-run.
+# fd66::/48 is never given a next hop of the ROS gateway.
+set -euo pipefail
+del_rule() {
+  while "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; do :; done || true

+# rp_filter=2 and no ICMP redirects on Meridian's interfaces only (the
+# managed tunnels, the interface the topology names, mra/mmesh). The kernel
+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the
+# interface value is what matters here. Other interfaces are not touched.
+harden_sysctl() {
+  local i
+  for i in "$@"; do
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.rp_filter=2" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.send_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv6.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  done
+}

+#!/bin/bash
+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='jp-a'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"
+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"
+run_rc() {
+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/
+probe grok https://grok.x.ai/

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+# The MTU each tunnel interface's config sets ("MTU ="): wg syncconf keeps the
+# running interface MTU, so an existing interface is aligned in place below.
+wg_conf_mtu() {
+  case "$1" in
+    m08) echo 1420 ;;
+    m15) echo 1420 ;;
+    m20) echo 1280 ;;
+    *) echo "" ;;
+  esac
+}
+for iface in m08 m15 m20; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+    want_mtu=$(wg_conf_mtu "$iface")
+    have_mtu=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$iface/mtu" 2>/dev/null || true)

+      ip link set dev "$iface" mtu "$want_mtu"
+      echo "meridian-wg-mtu: $iface ${have_mtu:-?} -> $want_mtu (set in place; the tunnel stays up)"
+    fi
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi

+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi

+  nd=/etc/systemd/networkd.conf.d/90-meridian.conf

+ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=no
+ManageForeignRoutes=no'

+    else

+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh

===== nodes/sg1/usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh (added) =====
+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-fb87aa3c
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m09 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m09 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m16 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m16 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='sg1'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"
+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"
+run_rc() {
+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/
+probe grok https://grok.x.ai/
+token_file=/etc/meridian/unlock-report.env
+if [ -f "$token_file" ] && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  tok=$(sed -n 's/^MERIDIAN_PANEL_TOKEN=//p' "$token_file" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
+  case "$tok" in
+    ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._~/+-]*)
+      echo "unlock report skipped: token missing or refused" >&2
+      ;;
+    *)
+      body=$(EXIT_ID="$exit_id" STARTED="$started" RAW4="$raw4" RAW6="$raw6" AI="$ai" python3 - <<'PY'
+import json, os
+def slurp(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as fh:
+            return fh.read()[-100000:]
+    except OSError:
+        return ""
+# raw4/raw6 are the -M 4 / -M 6 runs; the AI probes use curl -4.
+print(json.dumps({
+    "exit_id": os.environ["EXIT_ID"],
+    "kind": "scheduled",
+    "at": os.environ["STARTED"],
+    "family": "ipv4",
+    "raw4": slurp(os.environ["RAW4"]),
+    "raw6": slurp(os.environ["RAW6"]),
+    "ai": slurp(os.environ["AI"]),
+}))
+PY
+)
+      hdr=$(mktemp)
+      chmod 600 "$hdr"
+      printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$tok" > "$hdr"
+      curl --silent --show-error --max-time 20 --config "$hdr" \
+        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+        --data-binary "$body" \
+        "$panel/api/unlock/report" >/dev/null || true
+      rm -f "$hdr"
+      ;;
+  esac
+fi
+echo "unlock-probe-wrote $raw"

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+# The MTU each tunnel interface's config sets ("MTU ="): wg syncconf keeps the
+# running interface MTU, so an existing interface is aligned in place below.
+wg_conf_mtu() {
+  case "$1" in
+    m09) echo 1420 ;;
+    m16) echo 1420 ;;
+    *) echo "" ;;
+  esac
+}
+for iface in m09 m16; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+    want_mtu=$(wg_conf_mtu "$iface")
+    have_mtu=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$iface/mtu" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [ -n "$want_mtu" ] && [ "$have_mtu" != "$want_mtu" ]; then
+      ip link set dev "$iface" mtu "$want_mtu"
+      echo "meridian-wg-mtu: $iface ${have_mtu:-?} -> $want_mtu (set in place; the tunnel stays up)"
+    fi
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+if [ -e /lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ] || [ -e /usr/lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ]; then
+  nd=/etc/systemd/networkd.conf.d/90-meridian.conf
+  nd_want='# meridian: keep Meridian ip rules and routes when systemd-networkd restarts
+[Network]
+ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=no
+ManageForeignRoutes=no'
+  if [ "$(cat "$nd" 2>/dev/null)" != "$nd_want" ]; then
+    if mkdir -p "${nd%/*}" && printf '%s\n' "$nd_want" > "$nd.tmp" && chmod 0644 "$nd.tmp" && mv -f "$nd.tmp" "$nd"; then
+      echo "meridian-networkd: wrote $nd (networkd not restarted; it applies at its next start)"
+    else
+      rm -f "$nd.tmp"
+      echo "meridian-networkd: could not write $nd; a networkd restart would delete the Meridian ip rules" >&2
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit meridian-unlock.timer
+if [ -f /etc/smartdns/smartdns.conf ] && [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  if systemctl cat meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    systemctl enable meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    systemctl restart meridian-smartdns.service || echo "meridian-smartdns.service restart failed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  else
+    echo "meridian-smartdns.service is not installed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  fi
+fi
+echo meridian-up-complete

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-1b224e02
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m19 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m19 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+)
+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Policy routes for one Meridian node. Safe to re-run.
+# fd66::/48 is never given a next hop of the ROS gateway.
+set -euo pipefail
+del_rule() {
+  while "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; do :; done || true
+}
+# rp_filter=2 and no ICMP redirects on Meridian's interfaces only (the
+# managed tunnels, the interface the topology names, mra/mmesh). The kernel
+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the
+# interface value is what matters here. Other interfaces are not touched.
+harden_sysctl() {
+  local i
+  for i in "$@"; do
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.rp_filter=2" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.send_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    sysctl -w "net.ipv6.conf.${i}.accept_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  done
+}
+harden_sysctl eth0 m19

+#!/bin/bash
+# Streaming/AI probe for one exit. Run on the exit, never on the home gateway.
+# lmc999/regioncheck stays an independent container (AGPL-3.0). Its published
+# ENTRYPOINT is "bash -lc /check.sh", which drops extra arguments and then
+# reads an interactive region menu. Override the entrypoint and pass -R 66
+# (all platforms) plus -M 4 and -M 6 so a timer cannot block on read().
+# The panel token is read from /etc/meridian/unlock-report.env (mode 0600).
+# It is not written into this file, and the URL is not taken from that file.
+set -u
+exit_id='twnat'
+image='lmc999/regioncheck:latest'
+panel='http://192.168.77.2:8787'
+dir=/var/lib/meridian
+mkdir -p "$dir"
+# When the probe started. The panel orders reports by this time (a late
+# report cannot overwrite a newer one) and rejects reports older than one
+# hour; its 30-minute return cooldown still runs on the panel's own clock.
+started=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
+raw="$dir/unlock-last.txt"
+raw4="$dir/unlock-last-v4.txt"
+raw6="$dir/unlock-last-v6.txt"
+ai="$dir/unlock-ai.txt"
+: > "$raw4"
+: > "$raw6"
+run_rc() {
+  family="$1"; out="$2"
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck container is not installed" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "regioncheck image is not present locally: $image" >> "$out"
+    echo "pull it on this exit with: docker pull $image" >> "$out"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 25m docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint /check.sh \
+    "$image" -R 66 -M "$family" -E en >> "$out" 2>&1 || true
+}
+run_rc 4 "$raw4"
+run_rc 6 "$raw6"
+cat "$raw4" "$raw6" > "$raw"
+: > "$ai"
+probe() {
+  id="$1"; url="$2"
+  code=$(curl -4 -o /dev/null -s -m 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)
+  [ -n "$code" ] || code=000
+  echo "$id $code" >> "$ai"
+}
+probe openai https://chatgpt.com/
+probe anthropic https://claude.ai/
+probe gemini https://gemini.google.com/
+probe copilot https://copilot.microsoft.com/
+probe perplexity https://www.perplexity.ai/
+probe grok https://grok.x.ai/
+token_file=/etc/meridian/unlock-report.env
+if [ -f "$token_file" ] && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  tok=$(sed -n 's/^MERIDIAN_PANEL_TOKEN=//p' "$token_file" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
+  case "$tok" in
+    ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._~/+-]*)
+      echo "unlock report skipped: token missing or refused" >&2
+      ;;
+    *)
+      body=$(EXIT_ID="$exit_id" STARTED="$started" RAW4="$raw4" RAW6="$raw6" AI="$ai" python3 - <<'PY'
+import json, os
+def slurp(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as fh:
+            return fh.read()[-100000:]
+    except OSError:
+        return ""
+# raw4/raw6 are the -M 4 / -M 6 runs; the AI probes use curl -4.
+print(json.dumps({
+    "exit_id": os.environ["EXIT_ID"],
+    "kind": "scheduled",
+    "at": os.environ["STARTED"],
+    "family": "ipv4",
+    "raw4": slurp(os.environ["RAW4"]),
+    "raw6": slurp(os.environ["RAW6"]),
+    "ai": slurp(os.environ["AI"]),
+}))
+PY
+)
+      hdr=$(mktemp)
+      chmod 600 "$hdr"
+      printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$tok" > "$hdr"
+      curl --silent --show-error --max-time 20 --config "$hdr" \
+        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+        --data-binary "$body" \
+        "$panel/api/unlock/report" >/dev/null || true
+      rm -f "$hdr"
+      ;;
+  esac
+fi
+echo "unlock-probe-wrote $raw"

+#!/bin/bash
+# Bring up Meridian on this host without flushing the rest of nftables.
+# A bad line in sysctl is skipped so a wrong interface name cannot abort SSH.
+# Normally run by meridian.service (boot, and activation via meridian-host).
+set -euo pipefail
+# meridian-wan: eth0 set need=4
+MERIDIAN_NFT=/etc/nftables.d/meridian.nft
+if [ -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT" ]; then
+  if ! nft -c -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-check-failed: running ruleset left unchanged; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ! nft -f "$MERIDIAN_NFT"; then
+    echo "meridian-nft-load-failed: the batch was aborted as a whole; previous Meridian tables kept; routes and forwarding not touched" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+if [ -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf ]; then
+  sysctl_ok=0; sysctl_skip=0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    case "$line" in ''|'#'*|*ip_forward=*|*.forwarding=*) continue ;; esac
+    if sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1; then sysctl_ok=$((sysctl_ok + 1)); else sysctl_skip=$((sysctl_skip + 1)); echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2; fi
+  done < /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: applied $sysctl_ok, skipped $sysctl_skip from /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf"
+else
+  echo "meridian-sysctl: /etc/sysctl.d/99-meridian.conf missing; host sysctls not applied" >&2
+fi
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh ]; then
+  if ! /usr/local/sbin/meridian-fwcompat.sh apply; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: the host's FORWARD policy drops tunnel traffic and Meridian's DOCKER-USER rules could not be ensured; forwarding not enabled, tunnels not brought up" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+MERIDIAN_FWD=/etc/meridian/forwarding.conf
+if [ ! -f "$MERIDIAN_FWD" ]; then
+  echo "meridian-forwarding-missing: $MERIDIAN_FWD not found; forwarding left as is" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
+  case "$line" in
+    net.ipv4.ip_forward=*|net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=*)
+      if ! sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "meridian-forwarding-failed: $line" >&2
+        exit 1
+      fi ;;
+    *) sysctl -w "$line" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "skip sysctl: $line" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+done < "$MERIDIAN_FWD"
+# The MTU each tunnel interface's config sets ("MTU ="): wg syncconf keeps the
+# running interface MTU, so an existing interface is aligned in place below.
+wg_conf_mtu() {
+  case "$1" in
+    m19) echo 1420 ;;
+    *) echo "" ;;
+  esac
+}
+for iface in m19; do
+  conf="/etc/wireguard/$iface.conf"
+  if [ ! -f "$conf" ]; then
+    echo "meridian-wg-missing: $conf is listed in this manifest but not installed" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  if ip link show "$iface" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    wg syncconf "$iface" <(wg-quick strip "$conf")
+    want_mtu=$(wg_conf_mtu "$iface")
+    have_mtu=$(cat "/sys/class/net/$iface/mtu" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [ -n "$want_mtu" ] && [ "$have_mtu" != "$want_mtu" ]; then
+      ip link set dev "$iface" mtu "$want_mtu"
+      echo "meridian-wg-mtu: $iface ${have_mtu:-?} -> $want_mtu (set in place; the tunnel stays up)"
+    fi
+  else
+    wg-quick up "$conf"
+  fi
+done
+if [ -x /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh ]; then
+  /usr/local/sbin/meridian-mesh-up.sh || echo "mesh sidecar skipped" >&2
+fi
+if [ -e /lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ] || [ -e /usr/lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service ]; then
+  nd=/etc/systemd/networkd.conf.d/90-meridian.conf
+  nd_want='# meridian: keep Meridian ip rules and routes when systemd-networkd restarts
+[Network]
+ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=no
+ManageForeignRoutes=no'
+  if [ "$(cat "$nd" 2>/dev/null)" != "$nd_want" ]; then
+    if mkdir -p "${nd%/*}" && printf '%s\n' "$nd_want" > "$nd.tmp" && chmod 0644 "$nd.tmp" && mv -f "$nd.tmp" "$nd"; then
+      echo "meridian-networkd: wrote $nd (networkd not restarted; it applies at its next start)"
+    else
+      rm -f "$nd.tmp"
+      echo "meridian-networkd: could not write $nd; a networkd restart would delete the Meridian ip rules" >&2
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+/usr/local/sbin/meridian-routes.sh
+enable_unit() {
+  if [ ! -d /run/systemd/system ] || ! command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-systemd-missing: cannot start $1 here; activate through meridian-host on the host" >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  systemctl enable --now "$1"
+}
+enable_unit meridian-unlock.timer
+if [ -f /etc/smartdns/smartdns.conf ] && [ -d /run/systemd/system ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  if systemctl cat meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    systemctl enable meridian-smartdns.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    systemctl restart meridian-smartdns.service || echo "meridian-smartdns.service restart failed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  else
+    echo "meridian-smartdns.service is not installed; exit resolver is down" >&2
+  fi
+fi
+echo meridian-up-complete

+#!/bin/bash
+# Meridian forwarding coexistence with a FORWARD policy of DROP (Docker).
+# Managed by Meridian (node manifest). It only adds ACCEPT rules for
+# Meridian's own interfaces at the top of DOCKER-USER, the chain Docker
+# reserves for the operator and jumps to first from FORWARD. It never
+# touches Docker's chains, never sets a policy and never flushes anything:
+# every rule it adds carries the tag below, and only tagged rules are ever
+# deleted. A family (iptables / ip6tables) whose FORWARD policy is not DROP
+# gets no rule. Run by meridian-up.sh and by meridian-fwcompat.service each
+# time docker.service (re)starts.
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh apply    add the missing rules, remove stale tagged ones
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh remove   remove every Meridian-tagged rule
+#   meridian-fwcompat.sh status   print the tagged rules present
+set -u
+FW_TAG=meridian-fw-07354b30
+FW_CHAIN=DOCKER-USER
+FW_RULES=(
+  "-i m10 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m10 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"
+  "-i m17 -o eth0"
+  "-i eth0 -o m17 -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED"

+m_fw_tool() { case "$1" in 4) echo iptables ;; 6) echo ip6tables ;; esac; }
+# m_fw_tagged FAM: the -S lines of DOCKER-USER that carry a Meridian tag.
+m_fw_tagged() {
+  local tool out
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$1")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S DOCKER-USER 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E -- '^-A DOCKER-USER .*--comment "?meridian-fw-[0-9a-f]{8}"?( |$)' || true
+}
+# m_fw_remove_tagged FAM KEEP: delete every tagged rule except those tagged KEEP.
+m_fw_remove_tagged() {
+  local fam=$1 keep=$2 tool line rc=0
+  local -a args
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
+    if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
+      case " $line " in *" --comment $keep "*) continue ;; esac
+    fi
+    set -f
+    read -r -a args <<< "$line"
+    set +f
+    args[0]=-D
+    if "$tool" -w 5 "${args[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam removed ${line#-A }"
+    else
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not remove IPv$fam ${line#-A }" >&2
+      rc=1
+    fi
+  done < <(m_fw_tagged "$fam")
+  return $rc
+}
+fw_apply_family() {
+  local fam=$1 tool pol out i rc=0 line
+  local -a spec
+  tool=$(m_fw_tool "$fam")
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  if ! out=$("$tool" -w 5 -S FORWARD 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: $tool -S FORWARD failed; rules left as they are" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  # The policy line, not the first line: iptables-nft may print a comment
+  # ("# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present …") before it.
+  pol=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m 1 -- '^-P FORWARD ' || true)
+  case "$pol" in
+    "-P FORWARD DROP") ;;
+    "-P FORWARD ACCEPT")
+      # Nothing to work around in this family: no rule of ours belongs here.
+      m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" ""
+      return $? ;;
+    *)
+      echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: IPv$fam FORWARD policy unreadable ($pol); rules left as they are" >&2
+      return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  if ! "$tool" -w 5 -S "$FW_CHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "meridian-fwcompat-unsupported: IPv$fam FORWARD policy is DROP and there is no $FW_CHAIN chain (not Docker, or Docker without its iptables rules); forwarded tunnel traffic is dropped, nothing was changed" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for ((i=${#FW_RULES[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
+    set -f
+    read -r -a spec <<< "${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+    set +f
+    if ! "$tool" -w 5 -C "$FW_CHAIN" "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      if "$tool" -w 5 -I "$FW_CHAIN" 1 "${spec[@]}" -m comment --comment "$FW_TAG" -j ACCEPT; then
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat: IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN + ${FW_RULES[$i]}"
+      else
+        echo "meridian-fwcompat-failed: could not insert into IPv$fam $FW_CHAIN: ${FW_RULES[$i]}" >&2
+        rc=1
+      fi
+    fi
+  done
+  # Rules of an earlier rule set (another tag) go; the current set stays.
+  m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "$FW_TAG" || rc=1
+  return $rc
+}
+# meridian-node.service and meridian-fwcompat.service can both run at boot:
+# one at a time, so a check-then-insert cannot add a rule twice.
+fw_lock() {
+  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -w /run ]; then
+    exec 9>>/run/meridian-fwcompat.lock || return 0
+    flock -w 30 9 || true
+  fi
+}
+rc=0
+case "${1:-apply}" in
+  apply)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do fw_apply_family "$fam" || rc=1; done ;;
+  remove)
+    fw_lock
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_remove_tagged "$fam" "" || rc=1; done ;;
+  status)
+    for fam in 4 6; do m_fw_tagged "$fam" | sed "s/^/IPv$fam /"; done ;;
+  *) echo "usage: $0 apply|remove|status" >&2; rc=2 ;;
+esac
+exit $rc

+#!/bin/bash
+# Policy routes for one Meridian node. Safe to re-run.
+# fd66::/48 is never given a next hop of the ROS gateway.

+# rp_filter=2 and no ICMP redirects on Meridian's interfaces only (the
+# managed tunnels, the interface the topology names, mra/mmesh). The kernel
+# uses max(all, iface) for rp_filter and ORs send_redirects, so the
+# interface value is what matters here. Other interfaces are not touched.
+harden_sysctl() {
+  local i

+    sysctl -w "net.ipv4.conf.${i}.send_redirects=0" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
